- [ ] **TS-504-followup-2a-1a** — The portal browser SDK: a consent decision, not a config default — **USER-BLOCKED**

  - The server and edge runtimes now report (TS-504-followup-2a-1). The browser does not, and that is
    deliberate: `@sentry/nextjs`'s client SDK ships **session replay** and **DOM-interaction breadcrumbs**,
    and these portals render a named senior's care schedule, wellness notes and household roster. Recording
    that in a third-party processor is a §12 / PDD §16.3 consent question.
  - **What is actually being asked**, so the decision can be made rather than deferred again:
    1. Client-side _error_ reporting only (no replay, no DOM breadcrumbs) — catches the errors a family
       actually sees, and the scrubbers already apply. This is the narrow option and probably the right one.
    2. Error reporting _plus_ replay — materially better debugging, and a recording of a senior's care
       record rendered in a browser leaving the platform.
    3. Nothing. The server half already carries most failures worth having.
  - Option 1 is not free either: a browser breadcrumb trail includes URLs, and portal URLs carry household
    and senior ids. `scrubUrl` / `scrubQueryString` handle query strings, **not path segments** — so if
    option 1 is chosen, path-segment redaction is part of the work, not a follow-up to it.
  - The scrubbers and `portalSentryOptions` are already shared and would apply unchanged; the work is a
    client config per portal plus whichever redaction the decision requires.
  - Acceptance: the decision is recorded with its reason (including "no"), and if it is yes, the chosen
    option ships with replay explicitly configured rather than defaulted, and
    `observability-wiring-coverage.test.ts`'s "ships no browser SDK" assertion is replaced by one that
    pins what _was_ decided — never simply deleted.
  - References: CLAUDE.md §12, §10, §17.2; PDD §16.3; TS-504-followup-2a-1

- [ ] **TS-505b** — E2E: household + senior + subscription — **USER-BLOCKED on the Stripe stub decision**

  - TS-505a's harness makes adding a slice mechanical: one entry in `apps/e2e/src/fleet.ts` per service, one spec file. `service-household` needs nothing new. **`service-subscription` does**, and it is a decision, not an implementation: activating a subscription requires Stripe. Two halves, with different answers:
    - **Inbound (webhook).** Already solvable with no new dependency — `service-webhook` verifies with `stripe.webhooks.constructEvent`, and the suite holds the signing secret, so it can sign a `checkout.session.completed` payload itself. This is the honest path anyway: a real subscription activates on a webhook.
    - **Outbound (creating the checkout session).** `StripeModule` calls the live API and the SDK's host is not configurable from env. Options, none silently pickable (CLAUDE.md §16): (1) run `stripe/stripe-mock` as a docker-compose profile + add a `STRIPE_API_BASE` override to `service-subscription`'s env; (2) skip session creation in the suite and drive activation from a signed webhook against a pre-seeded row — cheaper, but leaves the platform's own checkout-session code path unexercised; (3) `stripe-mock` in CI only.
  - Acceptance: signup → verified account → household + senior → an **active** subscription, asserted through the gateway; the Stripe seam's shape recorded in the entry before any code lands.
  - References: CLAUDE.md §9.1, §13, §16; `apps/service-subscription/src/modules/stripe/stripe.module.ts`; `apps/e2e/README.md`

- [ ] **TS-505c-followup-1a** — Confirm a single green root `pnpm turbo run build` on a clean machine

  - TS-505c-followup-1 removed the build's dependency on `API_GATEWAY_BASE_URL` and verified **each** of
    web-admin, web-family and web-provider building green with the variable unset. What could not be
    demonstrated on this machine is the whole thing in one command.
  - The blocker is the environment, not the change: the pnpm virtual store on this box goes hollow
    repeatedly, and it does so **between builds within a single run** — a bulk relink is followed by one or
    two successful Next builds, then `next`, then `styled-jsx`, then `@swc/helpers`, then `@next/env` in turn.
    Sequential (`--concurrency=1`) fails the same way, so concurrency is not the cause, and the Prisma
    postinstall that the repair recipe prescribes was tested and cleared as a suspect.
  - So the acceptance criterion is really a **CI** question now. It should be cheap to answer: a root
    `pnpm turbo run build` on a clean runner with no gateway env set.
  - Note this is also the natural place to confirm the image builds, which is the part that actually mattered
    — the three portal Dockerfiles run the same `next build` with no gateway URL.
  - Acceptance: one green root build and one green portal image build, on CI, with no `API_GATEWAY_BASE_URL`.
  - References: CLAUDE.md §11; `infra/docker/nextjs.Dockerfile`; TS-505c-followup-1

- [ ] **TS-505d2-followup-1a** — No test anywhere proves a produced event reaches its consumer

  - TS-505d2-followup-1 was a defect with green tests on both sides: `service-search` had unit tests proving
    it appends `search.result_clicked` to its outbox, `service-analytics` had unit tests proving its
    handler processes that event, and in a deployed cluster the event would never have arrived because the
    relay was not configured to drain the table between them. Every producer/consumer pair on the platform
    has this shape, and nothing exercises the seam.
  - The new `outbox-sources-coverage` guard closes the specific hole (a table nobody drains) but it is a
    static check on configuration — it cannot catch a stream-name mismatch, a consumer group that never
    subscribes, or a payload the consumer rejects at the boundary.
  - Shape: one E2E spec that drives a real produce → relay → consume round trip through the fleet
    (`apps/e2e` already boots the relay), asserting the consumer's landing row appears. One pair proves the
    transport; it does not need to be repeated per event.
  - Acceptance: an E2E spec fails if the relay is misconfigured for the producing schema, or if the
    consumer never receives a published event.
  - **PREMISE-CHECKED 2026-08-06 — the shape asked for here already exists, and this entry is stale.**
    `apps/e2e/tests/incident-booking-hold.spec.ts` (TS-505d2-followup-3b, landed after this entry was
    filed) drives exactly the round trip described: `service-trust-safety` appends
    `trust_safety.booking_hold.requested` inside the incident transaction, `worker-outbox-relay` drains it,
    and `service-booking`'s outbox consumer turns it into the `booking_subject_holds` row + `held_by_incident_id`
    stamp the spec then reads back **through the gateway**. Three processes and a real bus hop; the assertion
    is the consumer's landing row, not the event. `fleet.ts` lists `trust_safety.outbox_events` in
    `OUTBOX_SOURCES`, so removing it makes `waitForBookingHolds` time out and the spec fail — which is the
    first half of the acceptance. The spec's second case (a `medium` concern holds nothing, proven by waiting
    out a window in which a hold would certainly have landed) covers the "consumer never receives" direction.
  - **What is genuinely left is confirmation, not construction**: re-inject the misconfiguration (drop

- [ ] **TS-505d-prep-followup-1a** — `@Idempotent()` on a pre-auth route rests on the request-body hash alone

  - Found while closing TS-505d-prep-followup-1. `nest-idempotency`'s `defaultActorResolver` reads
    `request.requestContext.userId` and falls back to **`anonymous`** when there is none — which is every
    pre-auth route by definition. All anonymous callers therefore share one bucket, and the only thing
    keeping two of them apart is the `hashRequestBody` mismatch check (same key + different body → 409).
  - `signup` is safe: its body carries the email, so a collision needs an attacker who already knows it.
    **`refresh` would not be.** Its token rides a cookie, so its body is empty — two unrelated callers who
    picked the same `Idempotency-Key` hash identically, and the cached response being replayed is a token
    pair. The gateway now forwards the header on `refresh` (correctly — the value is the caller's and the
    edge is not where it should die), so the whole question is whether identity ever decorates that route.
  - This is a property of the **package**, not of any one route: `actorResolver` is a documented knob and the
    fix is probably a pre-auth resolver that mixes in something caller-specific, or a documented refusal to
    support `@Idempotent()` where the body does not distinguish callers.
  - Not urgent — nothing is decorated that way today, and a warning comment naming this entry sits on
    `AuthProxyController`. It becomes urgent the moment someone decorates `refresh` or `logout`.
  - Acceptance: either a pre-auth actor segment that separates callers, or a stated rule (with a guard) that
    `@Idempotent()` may not be applied to a route whose body can be empty.
  - References: CLAUDE.md §3.1, §3.3; `packages/nest-idempotency/src/store/key.ts`;
    `packages/nest-idempotency/src/config.ts`; `apps/api-gateway/src/modules/gateway-routes/auth-proxy.controller.ts`

- [ ] **TS-505d-prep-followup-1b** — The gateway still has no idempotency cache of its own (TS-140-followup-5)

  - TS-505d-prep-followup-1 established that the gateway forwards the caller's key so the downstream's
    `@Idempotent()` has something to key on. That is the right layering and it closes the reported defect,
    but it leaves the **edge itself** uncached: a retry of a write whose downstream does NOT wear
    `@Idempotent()` still reaches the service twice.
  - Two proxy doc-comments had been deferring to this cache as though it existed, which is how the checkout
    and auth omissions survived review. Both now say plainly that it does not.
  - Worth scoping before building: it may be that per-route downstream decorators are the whole answer and
    the gateway cache is redundant (that was the original TS-140 reasoning). The decision, either way, should
    be recorded rather than left as a deferred follow-up nobody re-examines.
  - Acceptance: either `@taste-and-see/nest-idempotency` mounted on the gateway's write proxies, or a
    recorded decision that downstream decoration is sufficient, with the stale references removed.
  - References: CLAUDE.md §3.3, §17.5; `apps/api-gateway/src/app.module.ts`; `apps/api-gateway/src/redis/redis.module.ts`

- [ ] **TS-505-followup-2** — Browser-level E2E over the four portals

  - The suite is API-level by design (see `apps/e2e/README.md`). A browser slice is additive, not a replacement: it should assert what only a browser can — that the portal's server actions set their own cookies correctly, that senior-mode survives a reload, that a form's Zod resolver and the backend's agree. It must NOT re-assert the backend transitions the API specs already cover, through a slower and flakier lens.
  - Needs `playwright install` and the four Next.js apps built and served, so it belongs in its own CI job with its own browser cache.
  - References: CLAUDE.md §8.3, §8.5, §9.1

- [ ] **TS-510-followup-1a** — The token-prune scan has no index that serves it

  - Found 2026-08-02 while building TS-510-followup-1. That entry claimed "the `(user_id, consumed_at)` index already serves the scan". It does not: the prune predicate is `created_at < :cutoff AND (consumed_at IS NOT NULL OR expires_at < :now)`, which never mentions `user_id`, so the existing index's leading column is useless to it and Postgres will seq-scan `email_verification_tokens` on every tick.
  - It is not urgent — the sweep runs every 6 hours off the request path, and the table is small until signup volume grows — which is exactly why it is filed rather than fixed under the wrong task. Do it when there is a row count worth an `EXPLAIN ANALYZE`, and put that output in the PR body per CLAUDE.md §7.3.
  - Acceptance: an expand-only migration adding an index on `created_at` (a partial index `WHERE consumed_at IS NOT NULL` covers only half the OR, so measure before choosing); `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` in the PR body showing the plan change at realistic scale.
  - References: `apps/service-identity/src/modules/auth/services/verification-token-prune.service.ts`; CLAUDE.md §4.1, §7.3

- [ ] **TS-506-followup-3a** — Ten boot guards each walk `apps/` + `apps/workers/` with their own `readdirSync`

  - `packages/testing/src/boot/` now has ten files that enumerate the fleet from the filesystem, each with a
    private copy of the same two-scope walk (`apps/*` plus `apps/workers/*`, skipping the `workers` directory
    itself). The copies have already started to disagree about what they skip: `boot-graph-coverage` keys off
    `src/app.module.ts`, `env-example-coverage` off `src/config/env.ts` **or** `lib/env.ts` (so it sees the
    portals), `service-ports` off something else again. Those differences are mostly deliberate — the guards
    ask about different populations — but nothing distinguishes a deliberate difference from a copy that was
    never updated, which is the same problem `STUB_ENV` had.
  - The history says this matters: `apps/workers/*` was missed by three separate sweeps before
    TS-505-followup-4 precisely because each sweep re-derived its own list.
  - Suggested shape: one `src/boot/workspaces.ts` exporting the raw walk plus named predicates
    (`nestApps()`, `envSchemaOwners()`, `portals()`), so a guard declares _which population_ it covers instead
    of re-deriving it. The floor assertions stay per-guard — they are what catches a walk that stopped
    matching, and centralising them would put every guard's vacuity check in one place where one wrong edit
    disables all ten.
  - Deliberately NOT done inside TS-506-followup-3: a change touching ten existing guards is a different
    review from adding one, and mixing them would have hidden the new guard's own verification.
  - Acceptance: the two-scope walk exists once; each guard names the population it covers; every guard keeps
    its own floor assertion; the suite is green with no behaviour change (verify by re-injecting one defect
    per guard population, not by trusting the refactor).
  - References: CLAUDE.md §9.3; TS-506; TS-506-followup-2; TS-505-followup-4

- [ ] **TS-009f-followup-1** — Per-service OpenAPI drift gate once `@nestjs/swagger` is wired

  - Acceptance: today TS-009f checks one artifact — `packages/contracts/generated/openapi.json` — built from the Zod source-of-truth via `@asteasolutions/zod-to-openapi`. Once individual Nest services adopt `@nestjs/swagger` (PDD §26.2: "OpenAPI specs generated from NestJS via `@nestjs/swagger`"), each service should ship its own `generated/openapi.json` + a `check` script that diffs the service-emitted spec against the committed artifact. The reusable shape lives in `packages/contracts/src/openapi/cli.ts` — service-side can import the same drift detector. CI extends `contract-check` to invoke each service's `check` script (still scoped via turbo filter so we don't fan out the workspace build chain). Lands when the first Nest service exposes a stable OpenAPI surface for partner integration (likely with TS-400 partner portal or earlier if internal admin tooling needs published specs).
  - References: PDD.md §26.2; CLAUDE.md §5.3.

- [ ] **TS-009f-followup-2** — Wire the contract-check gate into branch protection

  - Acceptance: repo Settings → Branches → `main` lists "Contract drift (packages/contracts)" under "Require status checks to pass before merging" alongside the eight existing gates. Repo-settings change, not a code change — coordinate with the user since it requires admin permissions on the repo. Twin of TS-009d-followup-2 / TS-009g-followup-7.
  - References: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` `contract-check` job; CLAUDE.md §11.

- [ ] **TS-009f-followup-3** — Breaking-vs-additive change detection on contract diffs

  - Acceptance: when contract-check detects drift between the committed and regenerated artifact, a follow-on step runs `oasdiff` (or equivalent) against the previous main's artifact and the PR's artifact, then comments on the PR distinguishing additive (new schema, new endpoint, new optional field) from breaking (removed field, changed type, narrowed enum). Today the gate forces engineers to regenerate + commit the artifact, but doesn't differentiate "we added a field" (downstream consumers fine to ship later) from "we removed a field" (downstream consumers break at runtime). Lands once a second contract version exists in git history (today TS-009f's first commit is also the first artifact), so there's a previous main artifact to diff against.
  - References: CLAUDE.md §5.1 (versioning policy — "never break v1"); PDD §5.1.

  - Acceptance: TS-009f's original acceptance criterion called for "contract diff verification across consuming apps and services" — today's gate covers the upstream side (the contracts package itself), not the downstream side (every app/service that imports `@taste-and-see/contracts` runtime-validates incoming payloads against the shape). A follow-up wires Pact-style contract tests (CLAUDE.md §9.1 "Contract: every service's published events and APIs against `packages/contracts`") that record each consumer's actual payload usage and replay it against the latest contracts at CI time. Lands once Pact or schema-based contract tooling is on the approved-libraries list (today neither is in CLAUDE.md §13 — needs an ADR before adding).
  - References: CLAUDE.md §9.1; PDD.md §24.1.

- [ ] **TS-009g-followup-2a** — Bot-PAT so the promotion PR's own checks fire pre-merge

  - Acceptance: `.github/workflows/promote-overlay.yml` opens its PR with the built-in `GITHUB_TOKEN`, and GitHub's recursion guard means that PR does NOT auto-trigger `ci.yml` / `kubernetes-validate.yml` — so today the promotion is validated by the in-workflow `kubectl kustomize --enable-helm` render plus the `kubernetes-validate` push-trigger on the merge commit, not by the PR's own check suite pre-merge. Provision a least-privilege machine-user PAT (or a GitHub App installation token) stored as a repo secret, and switch the `gh pr create` step + branch push to use it so the PR is attributed to a non-`GITHUB_TOKEN` identity and its checks run before a human merges. Needs the user to mint + store the token (secret-management, not a code-only change). Until then the header caveat in `promote-overlay.yml` documents the manual "push an empty commit / close-reopen" workaround.
  - References: `.github/workflows/promote-overlay.yml` header § "GITHUB_TOKEN PR-CHECK CAVEAT"; CLAUDE.md §11; TS-009g-followup-3.

- [ ] **TS-009g-followup-3** — PR-time image build (no push) for early validation

  - Acceptance: a new job in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (or a per-service workflow extension) builds each touched service's image on every PR — `push: false` so no registry tags land — to surface Dockerfile / dependency regressions during PR review rather than at merge time. The build reuses BuildKit's GHA cache so the marginal latency is bounded (≤ 60s warm). Held off in TS-009g to keep PR latency low; lands when the merge-time-only signal is no longer sufficient.
  - References: `.github/workflows/service-identity-build.yml` header rationale.

- [ ] **TS-009g-followup-5** — Multi-arch image build (linux/amd64 + linux/arm64)

  - Acceptance: the reusable `build-push-image.yml` adds a `platforms: linux/amd64,linux/arm64` input (defaulting to amd64-only to preserve current behaviour) and wires `docker/setup-qemu-action` so the buildx step cross-compiles. Lands when (a) Apple Silicon dev becomes a meaningful share of contributors and `colima` users want native arm64 image pulls, OR (b) a Phase-3 cluster on Graviton (or equivalent arm64) targets the image. The Dockerfile is already arch-portable; only the build wiring needs to grow.
  - References: PDD §20.1 (container strategy); CLAUDE.md §11.

- [ ] **TS-009g-followup-6** — Cosign key-based signing alternative

  - Acceptance: a parallel signing flow using a long-lived KMS-backed key (rather than keyless OIDC) lands behind a workflow input. Useful when ops needs to verify signatures without depending on Sigstore Fulcio's certificate transparency (closed-environment customers; air-gapped audit). Today keyless is the right default — captured up-front so the path has a named owner.
  - References: PDD §21.3 (key rotation); CLAUDE.md §3.5; `.github/workflows/build-push-image.yml` cosign step.

- [ ] **TS-009g-followup-7** — Wire branch protection so the per-service build is a required status check

Today the build only triggers on push to main (not on PR), so this depends on TS-009g-followup-3 (PR-time build) landing first OR a separate gated workflow that builds on PR specifically for the protection check. Twin of TS-009d-followup-2 (admin-permission repo settings change, not code).
  - References: CLAUDE.md §11; TS-009d-followup-2; TS-009g-followup-3.

- [ ] **TS-023-followup-1a** — Bootstrap MFA enrolment surface for admin staff (closes the gate's chicken-and-egg)

  - Acceptance: a magic-link or super-admin-issued one-time enrolment URL lets a staff user complete MFA enrolment WITHOUT first being able to log in. The TS-023-followup-1 gate refuses to issue a session to an admin-role-holder whose `users.mfa_enabled` is false; today the only way to enrol is via `POST /auth/mfa/totp/enroll`, which itself requires an authenticated session. Runbook for Phase 1 is "enrol MFA before promoting to admin"; this follow-up closes the gap so a lost-device or inherited-account scenario doesn't lock staff out permanently. Lands alongside TS-073 (Twilio brought online for transactional SMS, since the magic link is delivered out-of-band) and TS-126 (admin user management — super_admin issues the link).
  - References: `apps/service-identity/src/modules/auth/services/auth.service.ts` admin-MFA gate doc-comment; PDD.md §10.1; CLAUDE.md §3.1

  - Acceptance: `MfaService.verifyRecoveryCode` (and the generate/invalidate paths) publish `mfa.recovery_code_used` / `mfa.recovery_codes_generated` / `mfa.recovery_codes_invalidated` domain events through the TS-142 outbox so `service-audit` (TS-100) records an immutable, hash-chained entry per CLAUDE.md §3.6. Today the events are emitted as structured `logger.log` lines in the audit-event shape (the TS-126-followup-5 "log now, wire the cross-service pipe when service-identity grows an outbox producer" precedent). Lands when service-identity adopts the `@taste-and-see/nest-outbox` producer (paired with TS-026-followup-3 / TS-126-followup-5, all of which want the same outbox wiring in this service).
  - References: PDD.md §7.3, §17.1; CLAUDE.md §3.6, §5.3; `apps/service-identity/src/modules/auth/services/mfa.service.ts` `verifyRecoveryCode`.

- [ ] **TS-023-followup-2b** — Real `service-notification` dispatch on recovery-code use

  - Acceptance: when a recovery code is consumed, a warmly-worded "a backup code was just used to sign in to your account" notification fires via `service-notification` (TS-073) — email always, SMS when the user has a verified phone — so the legitimate owner can react if it wasn't them, and a "you have N codes left, regenerate soon" nudge rides along when the remaining count is low. Today the intent is a structured `logger.log` line. Lands alongside TS-023-followup-2a (the outbox the dispatch consumes) or a direct notification-dispatch HTTP client in service-identity, whichever lands first (twin of TS-025-followup-3).
  - References: PDD.md §12.1; PRD.md §6.8; `apps/service-identity/src/modules/auth/services/mfa.service.ts` `verifyRecoveryCode`.

Pairs with an `api-gateway` proxy for `POST /api/v1/auth/mfa/recovery/verify` + the web-admin / web-family lost-device login UI (mirroring the TS-123 TOTP-verify proxy + `apps/web-admin/app/(public)/login/verify`). `MfaRecoveryCodeService.countRemaining` + `generate` already exist; this is the controller + gateway + UI wiring. - [ ] **TS-026-followup-1** — Migrate the synchronous webhook-dispatch hop to the TS-142 outbox relay

  - Acceptance: when TS-142 (outbox + relay) lands, the TS-026 synchronous HTTP POST from `service-webhook` to `service-identity` is replaced by a relay-consumed publication on the platform event bus. The `webhook.stripe_processed_events` row's `dispatched_at` continues to be the source of truth — once the relay marks it, the row is settled. `KYC_DISPATCH_URL` / `KYC_DISPATCH_API_KEY` / `KYC_DISPATCH_TIMEOUT_MS` become deprecated / unset and the `StripeIdentityKycDispatchService` is deleted (or converted into the relay's consumer-side handler). Captured here so the migration has a named owner — the synchronous shape is a deliberate pre-relay scaffolding (CLAUDE.md §5.3 "outbox pattern" is the eventual contract).
  - References: PDD.md §7.3 (outbox pattern); CLAUDE.md §5.3; TS-142; `apps/service-webhook/src/modules/stripe/services/kyc-dispatch.service.ts` module doc-comment.

- [ ] **TS-026-followup-2** — Backfill worker for `payload_key_version` rotation

  - Acceptance: a BullMQ scheduled / one-shot worker scans `identity.kyc_records WHERE payload_key_version < $configured_version AND payload_ciphertext IS NOT NULL`, re-wraps the payload under the new key, and updates the row in a single transaction per row. Lands the first time the KYC payload key actually rotates — today `KycPayloadCipherService.decrypt` is fail-closed on key-version mismatch, so a rotation without a backfill would make every KYC row's payload temporarily unreadable to admin tooling (TS-126 / TS-127). Captured up-front so the rotation runbook has a named owner. Mirrors TS-031-followup-3 / TS-032-followup-3 shape.
  - References: `apps/service-identity/src/modules/kyc/services/kyc-payload-cipher.service.ts` `decrypt` doc-comment (fail-closed rotation contract); CLAUDE.md §3.5.

- [ ] **TS-026-followup-3** — Domain event `kyc.status_changed` via outbox

  - Acceptance: every successful `applyWebhookEvent` that changes the row's status publishes `kyc.status_changed` (event id, userId, kycRecordId, externalId, previousStatus, nextStatus, verifiedAt) through the outbox pattern (transactional write of the event row alongside the row update). Consumers: `service-provider` (TS-051) — on transition into `verified`, automatically advance the provider's application from `in_review` → `active`; `service-notification` — warmly-worded confirmation email to the provider; `service-audit` (TS-100) — immutable log of the KYC outcome (PDD §16.3 / §17.1 / §17.2). Lands alongside TS-142 (outbox + relay infrastructure).
  - References: PDD.md §7.3, §17.1; CLAUDE.md §5.3.

- [ ] **TS-026-followup-4** — Provider-tier promotion hook on `kyc.status_changed`

  - Acceptance: once TS-051 (`service-provider` application flow + Checkr intake) and TS-052 (provider tier promotion) land, the `kyc.status_changed` consumer on the provider side advances `provider.status` from `in_review` → `active` when the KYC record transitions into `verified` AND the Checkr background check has also cleared. The combined gate is what PDD §11.1 + §16.2 describe — Stripe Identity light KYC is the cheap layer; Checkr is the deeper check; both gate tier promotion. Captured up-front so the cross-service contract has a named owner.
  - References: PRD.md §7.1; PDD.md §11.1, §16.2; TS-051; TS-052.

- [ ] **TS-026-followup-5** — Replace duck-typed Prisma row types with the canonical `@prisma/client` exports

- [ ] **TS-032-followup-5** — DB-level partial unique index closes the per-household-cap race window

  - Acceptance: a forward-compatible migration adds `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX emergency_contacts_household_active_unique_idx ON household.emergency_contacts(household_id) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL` is the WRONG shape (over-restrictive). The right shape is either a CHECK constraint that counts (Postgres does not support correlated CHECK) or a database-level trigger that rejects on cap-exceed. Lands when the count-then-insert race in `EmergencyContactsService.create` is observed in practice. Lower priority because at the 10-contact-per-household cap, a race is improbable (would require two concurrent creates within milliseconds of each other from the same household).

- [ ] **TS-041b-followup-3a-1** — An out-of-band plan change in Stripe leaves the local plan stale

  - TS-041b-followup-3a's reconciler deliberately does NOT own `planId` / `billingInterval`.
    Mapping a Stripe price back to a platform plan needs a reverse lookup that does not exist
    (`plans.stripe_product_id` is written lazily on first subscription, and nothing indexes
    price→plan). Guessing is the worse failure: the plan drives entitlement, so a wrong guess
    grants or removes a family's tier.
  - The likely shape is not "map it" but "detect and refuse": if the fetched subscription's price
    does not correspond to the local plan, record a distinct reconcile outcome and leave the row
    alone. That is the same posture as `unknown_status` — visibly stale beats confidently wrong.
  - Acceptance: a plan mismatch is detected and surfaced (metric + WARN) rather than silently
    ignored, OR a price→plan lookup lands and the reconciler owns the field. Either is acceptable;
    doing nothing is what this entry exists to stop.
  - References: `apps/service-subscription/src/modules/outbox-consumers/stripe-subscription-mapping.ts`
    (the `ReconcilableSubscriptionFields` doc-block enumerates every omission and its owner)

- [ ] **TS-041b-followup-3a-2** — A local subscription row whose Stripe object never existed is unreachable

  - The reconciler treats "no local row for this `sub_...`" as a no-op, which is right: only the
    creating request knows the `customerId` / `customerGroup` / `planId`. But the mirror case is
    real and currently invisible — if the Stripe create succeeded and the local write then failed,
    the platform holds a paid Stripe subscription it has no record of, and every subsequent
    webhook for it lands on `not_tracked` forever.
  - `subscription_stripe_reconcile_total{object="subscription",outcome="not_tracked"}` is the
    signal, and a trickle is NORMAL (out-of-band Dashboard activity), so the alert is on rate, not
    on presence. The fix is a reconciliation report, not an auto-create.
  - Acceptance: a scheduled comparison (or an ops read surface) that lists Stripe subscriptions
    with no local row, so the gap is enumerable rather than inferred from a counter.
  - References: TS-041b-followup-3a; CLAUDE.md §6

- [ ] **TS-041b-followup-4a** — One-off backfill of the payment-method display fields

  - TS-041b-followup-3c hydrates `brand` / `last4` / `expiry_month` / `expiry_year` on every future
    `payment_method.*` event, but a method attached BEFORE it shipped will not raise one again
    until something about the card changes — which for a working card may be years. Those rows stay
    null and the billing page keeps its gap for exactly the customers who have been here longest.
  - Shape: a one-off script (or a `@taste-and-see/nest-bullmq-scheduler` job that self-disables)
    that pages `payment_methods WHERE brand IS NULL`, retrieves each from Stripe and reuses
    `mapStripePaymentMethod` — the mapper is already pure and takes a `Stripe.PaymentMethod`, so
    the backfill shares the classification rules rather than restating them.
  - Rate-limit it. This is the one path that would fetch every payment method on the platform in a
    burst, and Stripe's read limit is shared with the live reconcilers.
  - Acceptance: rows with a resolvable Stripe method are hydrated; rows whose Stripe method is gone
    are LEFT ALONE and counted, not deleted (a detached-and-forgotten method is still referenced by
    subscription history).
  - References: `apps/service-subscription/src/modules/outbox-consumers/stripe-payment-method-mapping.ts`;
    TS-041b-followup-3c

- [ ] **TS-041a-followup-2a** — Retire the ingress tables' unused `dispatched_at` / partial index, or state what still uses it

  - `webhook.stripe_processed_events.dispatched_at` (and its Checkr twin) exist for the pre-relay
    synchronous dispatch hops. The Stripe one is now stamped by exactly one caller — the KYC hop
    (TS-026-followup-1 is the task to migrate that onto the relay). Once TS-026-followup-1 and
    TS-051-followup-1 land, no writer remains, and the column plus its partial index
    (`WHERE dispatched_at IS NULL`, TS-041a-followup-1) become a table-sized index over every row
    that has ever arrived, guarding nothing.
  - Do NOT drop it before those two land — the correct order is contract, not cleanup.
  - Acceptance: either the column + partial index are dropped in an expand→contract pair with the
    remaining writers gone, or the schema doc-comment names the writer that keeps it alive.
  - References: `apps/service-webhook/prisma/schema.prisma`; TS-026-followup-1; TS-051-followup-1; CLAUDE.md §4.1

- [ ] **TS-041a-followup-2b** — Nothing tells us Stripe started sending a billing type we do not relay

  - The relay allow-list is deliberately explicit (a prefix match would grow the bus surface silently),
    and `stripe_relay_appended_total` deliberately counts only the relayed branch — an event we never
    intended to relay is not a relay outcome. The gap that leaves: if Stripe introduces a new
    subscription/invoice event type, or an account enables a product that emits one, the platform ignores
    it and no signal anywhere says so.
  - The cheap version is NOT a `skipped` counter (most inbound traffic is skipped by design and the
    series would bury the three that matter). It is a periodic query over `webhook.stripe_processed_events`
    grouping `event_type` for types matching the billing object prefixes but absent from the allow-list —
    i.e. ask the ingress table, which already stores every type we have ever received.
  - Acceptance: a scheduled check (the `@taste-and-see/nest-bullmq-scheduler` shape) reports, at WARN,
    any received-but-unrelayed `customer.subscription.*` / `invoice.*` / `payment_method.*` type, with the
    count. Threshold-free — one occurrence is the whole signal.
  - References: `packages/contracts/src/events/stripe-billing.ts`; TS-041a-followup-2; CLAUDE.md §10

- [ ] **TS-041a-followup-3** — `stripe_processed_events` janitor worker

  - Acceptance: a BullMQ scheduled worker prunes `webhook.stripe_processed_events WHERE received_at < now() - retention_window`. Default retention window matches Stripe's own event retention (13 months — Stripe retains event payloads for 30 days for the Standard Connect tier and 13 months for the Custom / Express Connect tiers; we keep 13 months for safety). Configurable per environment. Lands once BullMQ infra is wired (TS-142 cross-cutting workers).
  - References: `apps/service-webhook/prisma/schema.prisma` `StripeProcessedEvent` doc-comment (retention); CLAUDE.md §4.1, §4.3.

     outside service-subscription able to see it. Four premise-check findings changed the build:
     (1) the shipped `subscription.payment_failed` contract required `invoiceId`+`amountUsdMinor` and its
     own producer holds NEITHER (driven by the handle-only `stripe.invoice.changed`) — deriving the amount
     from the plan price would disagree with the invoice on any proration/coupon, giving money a second
     source of truth against the ledger; both relaxed to optional, deliberately unpopulated, pinned by a
     test (safe: the contract had zero emitters AND zero consumers). (2) `graceUntil` — when THIS PLATFORM
     stops serving, vs `nextAttemptAt` = when STRIPE retries — was missing, and it is the field the
     dunning ladder needs; added required-but-nullable. (3) The pause `reason` is documented free-form text
     and on this platform is very often a health/bereavement disclosure about a named senior, so it does
     NOT cross the wire (`hasReason: boolean`; `.strict()` makes attaching it a rejected append rather than
     a silent fan-out to relay + Redis Streams + every consumer's dedup table). (4) `resumed.toStatus` is
     not always `active` — a subscription paused mid-dunning resumes to `past_due`.
     EVENT IDENTITY IS THREE RULES and the wrong one loses events: payment failed/succeeded key on
     `sourceEventId` (a subscription fails payment many times; a subscription-keyed id gives the ladder
     exactly one rung); exhaustion keys on the subscription (once per cycle; the caller is the hourly sweep
     passing a per-tick id); pause/resume key on the HISTORY ROW id — a test caught the first draft's

     pause would have been dropped at the outbox PK. Also: `OutboxService` is a REQUIRED ctor dep (an

     is what rolls back; new `outbox_validation_failed` → 500 (deploy skew, not a client fault) with its own
     metric label; `attemptsCleared` read PRE-update or every recovery reports clearing nothing; and
     `FakePrisma.$transaction` did not roll back at all, so the rollback assertion would have passed
     vacuously (fixed with a per-row deep copy — third sighting of this fake-Prisma bug).
     No migration, no infra change (`subscription.outbox_events` was already an `OUTBOX_SOURCES` entry), no

     ever dispatch. Each does a TWO-HOP JOIN worker-side: pull a batch from a source service over a
     shared-secret `/api/v1/internal/...` route → call service-identity

     a sibling service for this"). No `apps/service-*` calls notification at all; the gateway registers a
     'notification' key but proxies no route.

     family → `household.households.id`, provider → `provider.providers.id`, academy →

     product — there is NO householdId→userId or householdId→email resolver anywhere on the platform.
     service-household's existing internal batch deliberately returns `recipients: {userId, role}` and no
     emails ("those live in identity.users"). So a dunning consumer written today could receive the event
     and have nobody to send it to. → TS-042-followup-3a1 is the spine and everything else waits on it.

    land in the same change.

    before `timingSafeEqual` and the length equality is re-checked afterwards; a "simplification" that
    compares lengths first reintroduces the timing leak the padding exists to close.

     accumulated pause from BOTH numerator and denominator — with the same integer used for the extension
     — keeps the effective denominator identical to the original service duration, which is why every
     journal posted before the pause is still correct and no reversal + replacement pair is owed.
     Filed TS-042-followup-3b2-followup-1 (**the important one — a Stripe auto-resume emits no event, so
     the balance would stay paused forever**) and -2 (no metric on the new outcomes). See
     Completed_tasks.md. -->

  - Acceptance: `POST /api/v1/subscriptions/:id/pause` accepts an optional `resumesAt`, which is forwarded to Stripe as `pause_collection.resumes_at`. When that instant arrives **Stripe resumes collection on its own**. On this platform the only producer of `subscription.resumed` is `DunningService.resumeSubscription` (`apps/service-subscription/src/modules/subscriptions/services/dunning.service.ts:1014`) — the explicit operator/customer call.   - **Until this ships, do not advertise `resumesAt` on any customer-facing pause surface** — an auto-resume looks fine to the family and to Stripe while quietly halting revenue recognition on their subscription. The explicit resume path is complete and correct.

- [ ] **TS-042-followup-3b2-followup-2a-1** — A stuck balance can be seen and not unstuck

  - The paused queue (TS-042-followup-3b2-followup-2a) is read-only, and that is correct as shipped for the same reason TS-304-followup-3's hold queue has no lift endpoint: forcing a deferred-revenue balance back to `active` from the accounting side would restart amortisation on a subscription that service-subscription still considers paused, and the two would then disagree about the books. The honest repair for a balance stranded by a missed `subscription.resumed` is to **replay or re-emit the event from service-subscription**, not to mutate the balance.
  - So this is not "add a button". It is: decide what an operator does about a row on that queue, then build that. The candidates, in preference order — (a) an admin re-emit of `subscription.resumed` from service-subscription for a named subscription, which flows through the existing consumer and leaves the period extension correct; (b) a reconcile-now trigger that re-reads Stripe's `pause_collection` for the subscription (TS-042-followup-3b2-followup-1 already made the reconciler a producer, so this needs no new event); (c) nothing, and the queue stays a detection surface whose remedy is a runbook.
  - **Do not ship a direct status write on `deferred_revenue_balances`.** The recogniser owns that column's transitions and its pause arithmetic depends on `paused_at` / `paused_duration_seconds` moving together.
  - Acceptance: the chosen remedy exists and the queue page names it, or the entry is closed with (c) recorded as the decision and the runbook written.
  - References: `apps/service-accounting/src/modules/revenue-recognition/services/subscription-revenue-recognizer.service.ts`; `apps/service-subscription/src/modules/outbox-consumers/stripe-subscription-reconciler.service.ts`; TS-304-followup-3 (the read-only-queue precedent); CLAUDE.md §6, §17.7.

- [ ] **TS-042-followup-3b2-followup-2a-2** — The paused queue shows ids where a name is needed

  - Each row carries `subscriptionId`, `customerId` and `customerGroup` and nothing human. An operator triaging stranded revenue has to copy the subscription id into the subscriptions console to learn whose it is, and the `customerId` is a soft pointer whose target schema depends on the group (TS-042-followup-3a2a), so it cannot even be linked generically.
  - Same shape as TS-304-followup-3a (name resolution for held seniors/households) and it should be settled once for both: a gateway-side aggregation is the only place allowed to join across service schemas (§2.3), and **what may be shown is a privacy question, not a rendering one** — "which family's mother's care subscription is in trouble" is exactly the kind of fact §12 keeps off surfaces that do not need it. A link to the existing `/subscriptions/[id]` console may be the whole answer.
  - Acceptance: either the queue rows link into a surface that resolves the customer, or the entry records that ids are deliberate and why.
  - References: `apps/web-admin/app/(protected)/accounting/deferred-revenue/paused/page.tsx`; TS-304-followup-3a; CLAUDE.md §2.3, §12.

Consumers: `service-accounting` (contra-revenue entry on first invoice per PDD Appendix A), `service-analytics` (campaign attribution per PDD §9.3), `service-trust-safety` (welfare-monitoring signal — repeated coupon redemptions can indicate friend-fraud patterns). Lands alongside TS-142 (outbox + relay).
  - References: PDD.md §7.3, §9.3, §17.1; CLAUDE.md §5.3.

- [ ] **TS-043-followup-4** — Coupon-abuse pattern detection routed to trust & safety

  - Acceptance: a BullMQ scheduled worker scans the rate-limit Redis bucket history + the `coupon_redemptions` table for patterns indicative of abuse (e.g. one IP probing many codes against many accounts; one account redeeming many distinct codes in a short window; an account that redeems then cancels then re-redeems). Flagged patterns generate trust-safety tickets via `service-trust-safety`. Lands alongside TS-300 (trust & safety incident queue).
  - References: CLAUDE.md §12 "flag patterns to trust & safety"; PRD §10.4 fraud detection; TS-300.

  - Acceptance: once TS-142 routes verified Stripe events from `service-webhook` into this service, a new `coupons/handlers/coupon-webhook.handler.ts` subscribes to the three coupon events and reconciles the platform row. `coupon.deleted` is the load-bearing case: if ops deletes a Stripe Coupon outside the platform, the platform row's `stripe_coupon_id` becomes dangling; the handler flips `active=false` to defuse the next redemption. Idempotent on Stripe's `event.id`.
  - References: PDD.md §7.3 (relay), §11.1; CLAUDE.md §6.

Today the controller gates on authentication only (AccessTokenGuard) — row-level permission checks land with TS-052-followup-11's PermissionGuard lift to `packages/nest-auth`. Captured up-front so the admin tooling (TS-127) has named permissions to wire. Per the PDD Appendix B excerpt, `coupon:create` maps to `super_admin + marketing`; `coupon:deactivate` maps to `super_admin + marketing`.
  - References: PDD §10.4, Appendix B; CLAUDE.md §3.2; TS-052-followup-11.

POST /api/v1/admin/coupons → POST /api/v1/coupons/validate → POST /api/v1/subscriptions with `couponCode` → verify the Stripe Subscription carries a `discounts: [{coupon: ...}]` AND a Stripe Coupon exists in test mode AND the `coupon_redemptions` row landed AND `coupons.times_redeemed` incremented. Mirrors TS-026-followup-1's KYC migration shape.

  - Acceptance: a BullMQ scheduled / one-shot worker scans `provider.provider_background_checks WHERE payload_key_version < $configured_version AND payload_ciphertext IS NOT NULL`, re-wraps each payload under the new key, and updates the row in a single transaction. Lands the first time the background-check payload key actually rotates — today `BackgroundCheckPayloadCipherService.decrypt` is fail-closed on key-version mismatch, so a rotation without a backfill would make every payload temporarily unreadable to admin tooling. Mirrors TS-026-followup-2 / TS-031-followup-3 / TS-032-followup-3 shape.

  - Acceptance: every successful `submitApplication` publishes `provider.application_submitted` (event id, providerId, applicationId, userId, submittedAt). Every successful `applyWebhookEvent` that changes the row's status publishes `provider.background_check_status_changed` (event id, providerId, backgroundCheckId, previousStatus, nextStatus, completedAt). Both events use the outbox pattern (transactional write of the event row alongside the state change; relay process forwards). Consumers: `service-notification` (warmly-worded confirmation email on application; "your background check cleared" email on transition to `clear`); `service-audit` (immutable log per PDD §17.1); `service-trust-safety` (welfare-monitoring signal on `consider` outcomes). - [ ] **TS-052-followup-2** — Auto-evaluate tier on certification grant / revoke

  - Acceptance: the `CertificationsController.grantCertification` and `revokeCertification` handlers chain a `TierPromotionService.evaluateAndApply` call after the grant/revoke succeeds, applying any resulting tier transition in the same admin request. Today the controller leaves the two operations decoupled (admin must explicitly POST /tier/evaluate after a grant) — TS-052's decoupling is deliberate (PRD §5.2 implies ops may grant credentials in advance of a promotion) but the _ergonomic_ default for the happy path is "grant + auto-evaluate" via a query-string opt-in (`?autoEvaluate=true`) or a separate orchestration endpoint. Captured here so the admin tooling (TS-127) has a named handle when the UX requires it.
  - References: PRD §5.2; TS-127 admin subscription/provider management.

- [ ] **TS-052-followup-3** — Provider documents (food handler cert + insurance proof) via media-svc

These four document classes are a Phase-1 PRD requirement that hangs off the provider model. The `provider_documents` table (kind enum, signed-URL pointer to media-svc asset, reviewer signoff state, expiry) lands once `media-svc` (TS-110) is online for the mandatory upload pipeline (CLAUDE.md §3.4: magic-byte MIME + Sharp limitInputPixels + ClamAV). Captured up-front so the provider portal (TS-122) has a named integration point.
  - References: PRD §7.1, PDD §8.2 (provider_documents column inventory), PDD §21.5; TS-110.

- [ ] **TS-052-followup-4** — Demotion-on-expiry worker (gate cert lapse → tier drop)

  - Acceptance: a BullMQ scheduled worker scans `provider.provider_certifications WHERE expires_at < now() AND revoked_at IS NULL` (the partial index `provider_certifications_expires_at_idx` already covers this query) and, for each provider whose set of active gate codes changes, calls `TierPromotionService.evaluateAndApply` to apply the resulting demotion. Closes the lifecycle gap on PRD §9.3's 24-month renewal cadence — without the worker, a provider's tier never reflects an expired credential. Lands once BullMQ cross-cutting workers infra arrives (TS-142 / TS-022-followup-3 shape).
  - References: PRD §9.3, PDD §15.2; `apps/service-provider/prisma/schema.prisma` `provider_certifications_expires_at_idx`.

- [ ] **TS-052-followup-5** — Automatic tier evaluation on the combined-gate (KYC verified ∧ Checkr clear) event

  - Acceptance: when both TS-026-followup-3 (`kyc.status_changed` → verified) AND TS-051-followup-3 (`provider.background_check_status_changed` → clear) events have fired for a provider, the service-provider event consumer flips `providers.status` from `in_review` → `active` AND calls `TierPromotionService.evaluateAndApply` to compute the initial tier. This is the orchestration layer named in TS-026-followup-4 / TS-051-followup-4; TS-052 ships the tier-evaluation half so the orchestration has a target service to call. Lands alongside TS-142 (outbox + relay) and the two upstream events.
  - References: PRD §7.1; PDD §11.1, §16.2; TS-026-followup-4; TS-051-followup-4.

- [ ] **TS-052-followup-6** — Provider self-service certification withdrawal

  - Acceptance: a `DELETE /api/v1/providers/me/certifications/:certId` endpoint behind `AccessTokenGuard` + `@Idempotent()` lets a provider voluntarily withdraw a credential (e.g. on retirement from a specialty practice). The handler routes through `ProviderCertificationsService.revoke` with `revocation_reason = 'self_withdrawn'` and `revokerUserId = self`. Optional — most providers leave certs in place and let them lapse — but PRD §6.5 / §7.5 hint at provider-owned profile mutability. Lands with TS-122 (web-provider) when the portal UX needs it.
  - References: PRD §7.5; TS-122.

<!-- TS-053-followup-4a COMPLETE 2026-08-06, same day it was filed. The staleness TS-053-followup-4 shipped

     projector and consumed by the search-indexer's SEVENTH handler, which re-projects the discovery
     document.
     **The trigger is narrow ON PURPOSE and the code says so**: the projector runs on all five booking
     lifecycle events, and only `booking.completed` can move `bookings_completed`. Emitting on each would
     re-project an entire search document per booking transition to change an integer that did not change.
     Four parameterised tests assert the four non-emitting events, so widening the trigger by accident is a
     failing test rather than a quiet cost.
     **The event id is DETERMINISTIC** — `provider-metrics:{providerId}:{bookingId}` — so a redelivered
     completion produces the same id and the outbox's `ON CONFLICT (event_id) DO NOTHING` swallows it. The
     fact write is idempotent by `COALESCE` and now its announcement is idempotent by the same argument,
     rather than the consumer having to absorb a duplicate. Same shape as TS-308a's
     `impossible-travel:{prevId}:{curId}`.
     **The consumer does NOT use the payload's count.** It re-reads the snapshot like every other indexer
     handler (TS-053-followup-3), so a reordered redelivery cannot write an older number over a newer one —
     asserted by a test that checks `project()` is called with ONE argument.
     A refused append THROWS, rolling the fact write back: a projection that advanced while its announcement
     failed is the exact divergence this event exists to prevent. `OutboxValidationFailedError` is NOT
     exported by the SDK (it is a per-service local class — see `provider-certifications.service.ts`), so
     this producer names its own.
     Note the payload's `eventId` necessarily embeds the booking id; a test that first claimed "no booking
     id on the payload" was WRONG and was rewritten to state what is true — the payload's own fields are an
     identity and a number, and nothing about the household, the senior, the money or a cancellation reason
     rides along.
     service-provider 682 -> 692, search-indexer +3. GATE 188/188, contracts in sync.); see Completed_tasks.md. -->

- [ ] **TS-061-followup-1** — Full RFC 5545 RRULE coverage (BYDAY / BYMONTHDAY / WKST / BYSETPOS / RDATE / EXDATE / TZID / DAILY / YEARLY)

  - Acceptance: when product needs a recurring pattern outside the Phase-1 subset (e.g. "every second Tuesday of the month" → `FREQ=MONTHLY;BYDAY=2TU`), either extend the in-house expander or swap in the `rrule` npm library (requires approved-libraries addition per CLAUDE.md §13). The contract layer is already forward-compatible (stores the verbatim RRULE string up to 500 chars); only the expander needs to grow. Today the expander rejects every unsupported clause with `unsupported_clause` so a misconfigured series fails fast at create time.
  - References: PRD.md §6.3; `apps/service-booking/src/modules/recurrence/rrule-expander.ts` doc-comment (rejection list); CLAUDE.md §13.

- [ ] **TS-061-followup-2** — Series edit / cancel surfaces (per-occurrence + series-wide)

  - Acceptance: `PATCH /api/v1/bookings/recurring/:seriesId` adjusts the recurrence row (e.g. shorten COUNT, push UNTIL forward) and synthesises the matching child-row inserts / cancellations — atomic per series. `DELETE /api/v1/bookings/recurring/:seriesId` cancels every future occurrence (preserves completed children). Today the only series-mutation surface is per-child via `PATCH /api/v1/bookings/:id/status` (TS-060). Lands with TS-121 (web-family series-management UX) when the portal exposes the affordance.
  - References: PRD.md §6.3 (recurring booking modification); TS-121.

- [ ] **TS-061-followup-3** — Per-occurrence pricing override

  - Acceptance: a new optional `perOccurrenceOverrides: [{ index, basePriceMinor }]` field on `CreateRecurringBookingRequest` lets the family-portal price the Christmas Day visit differently from the regular Tuesday cadence. Today every materialised child carries the same money fields (Phase-1 product decision; cleaner contract surface). Lands when product justifies the complexity — usually a Tier 3 Concierge surface where holiday-rate pricing is in the consumer's mental model.
  - References: PRD.md §5.4, §6.6.

- [ ] **TS-062-followup-1** — Provider / actor authorization check on visit-notes write

  - Acceptance: `VisitNotesService.upsert` rejects when the authenticated `actorUserId` is not the booking's assigned provider (or, post-TS-128, an admin with the `booking:adjust` permission). Today the service trusts the controller's authenticated `userId` and stamps it as `recordedByUserId` for audit — mirrors the established Phase-1 booking pattern (`BookingsService` row-level access doc-comment). Lands once cross-service provider→user lookup is feasible via the gateway BFF (TS-140) or the TS-141 tenant-scoping Prisma extension. Sibling to TS-060-followup-1a.
  - References: CLAUDE.md §3.2; `apps/service-booking/src/modules/visit-notes/services/visit-notes.service.ts` row-level-access doc-comment; TS-141; TS-060-followup-1a.

- [ ] **TS-062-followup-2** — Domain event `booking.visit_notes_recorded` via outbox

  - Acceptance: every successful `VisitNotesService.upsert` publishes a `booking.visit_notes_recorded` event (event id, bookingId, visitNoteId, recordedByUserId, mood/appetite/hydration/socialEngagement enum levels, hasFreeform / hasPhotos flags — never the freeform body or photo keys) through the outbox pattern (transactional write of the event row alongside the upsert; relay forwards). Consumers: `service-trust-safety` (welfare-monitoring signal when persistently `none`/`poor`/`withdrawn` patterns across a senior's visits flag for ops review per PDD §16.1); `service-notification` (drives the monthly wellness summary email — PRD §6.9); `service-analytics` (per-tier wellness trend aggregates). The outbox append must run inside the same Prisma `$transaction` as the upsert — today the service writes directly without a transaction since there's no co-mutating side effect, but adding the event mandates the wrap. Lands alongside TS-142 (outbox + relay infrastructure).
  - References: PDD.md §7.3, §16.1, §17.1; PRD.md §6.9; CLAUDE.md §5.3.

  - Acceptance: the service rejects an upsert that carries a non-empty `photoKeys` array when the senior's photo-consent flag is not set (CLAUDE.md §12 "Senior consent gates ... default is opt-out"). Today the consent record doesn't exist as a column — the gate lands once TS-031-followup or a sibling task ships a `senior_consent` table with a `photos` boolean. Same shape as TS-033-followup-4 (memory-recipe images). Captured up-front so the gate has a named owner.
  - References: CLAUDE.md §12; PRD.md §6.4; PDD.md §16.3; TS-033-followup-4.

Today the contract validates the key shape only — a malicious client could supply an arbitrary S3 key the family-portal would render. Same defence-in-depth pattern as TS-033-followup-3.
  - References: CLAUDE.md §3.4, §17.16; PDD.md §21.5; TS-110; TS-033-followup-3.

The `completed` branch becomes "completed AND (now − completedAt) ≤ EDIT_WINDOW_MINUTES". Default window: 60 min. Lands when product defines the policy.
  - References: PRD.md §7.4; PDD.md §9.2; TS-065.

- [ ] **TS-064-followup-1** — Event-driven cache hydration via `subscription.tier_changed` + `provider.tier_changed`

  - Acceptance: when TS-142 lands the outbox + relay, a booking-side worker subscribes to `subscription.tier_changed` (emitted by service-subscription on plan flips) and `provider.tier_changed` (emitted by service-provider on tier promotions / demotions). Each consumer calls `TierGatingService.upsertHouseholdSnapshot` / `upsertProviderSnapshot` with the event's `eventId` as `sourceEventId` for idempotency-by-eventId. Today the snapshot rows hydrate only via the internal HTTP endpoints (ops / gateway). The event-driven path is the durable model; the HTTP endpoints stay as the manual override surface even after the events come online. Captured up-front so the cross-service contract has a named owner.
  - References: PDD.md §7.3 (outbox pattern); CLAUDE.md §5.3; TS-142.

- [ ] **TS-064-followup-2** — Flip `BOOKING_TIER_GATING_MODE` from `advisory` to `enforce` once snapshot coverage hits the threshold

  - Acceptance: once TS-064-followup-1 lands (event-driven hydration) AND the manual seeding runbook has backfilled every existing household + provider, the production env flips `BOOKING_TIER_GATING_MODE=enforce`. Gates the Tier-3-Concierge × non-Elite booking attempt at the service layer (CLAUDE.md §12). A short canary period in staging confirms there are no false rejections from stale snapshots before the flip. Phase-1 default is `advisory` because Phase-1 doesn't have full coverage yet.
  - References: CLAUDE.md §12; PRD.md §5.1, §5.2; TS-064-followup-1.

- [ ] **TS-064-followup-3** — OpenTelemetry tracing + Prometheus metrics for the tier-gating surface

The `BookingsService.createBooking` flow also emits `booking_tier_gating_violation_total{mode=enforce|advisory,reason=...}` on every violation (independent of the outbox event so the metric is dense in time even before the relay forwards). PII redacted at the logger and metric label level. Lands alongside `service-audit` (TS-100) where the shared `@taste-and-see/tracing` package gets its first real consumer. Mirrors TS-020-followup-1 / TS-060-followup-4 shape.

- [ ] **TS-065-followup-1** — Row-level access enforcement on dispute reads + mutations

  - Acceptance: `DisputesService.openDispute` / `getById` / `listByBookingId` / `updateDispute` reject when the authenticated `actorUserId` is not a household member of the booking's `householdId`, the booking's assigned provider, OR an admin-staff role-holder. Today the service trusts the controller-supplied `actorUserId` and records it on the row for audit. Lands once `service-household` exposes a cheap "is user X a member of household Y" gateway-aggregation endpoint AND `service-provider` exposes the "what's the user-id of this provider" lookup — without those, the check would require Cassandra-style joins that violate CLAUDE.md §2.3. Until then, TS-141 (tenant-scoping Prisma extension) lands first and the booking row's `householdId` / `providerId` become the audit trail. Mirrors TS-060-followup-1a / TS-062-followup-1 / TS-063-followup-1 shape.
  - References: CLAUDE.md §3.2, §17.10; `apps/service-booking/src/modules/disputes/services/disputes.service.ts` row-level-access doc-comment; TS-141; TS-064.

- [ ] **TS-065-followup-2** — Welfare-concern routing to `service-trust-safety`

  - Acceptance: when `booking.dispute_opened` lands with `reason = 'welfare_concern'`, the `service-trust-safety` consumer (TS-300) opens an incident ticket with severity ≥ `high`, blocks any future booking by the implicated provider pending review (PDD §16.1 automated holds), and routes into the mandated-reporter workflow (CLAUDE.md §12 — welfare concerns are first-class). The event already carries `reason` + `providerId` + `householdId` so the consumer can route without joining back. Lands alongside TS-300 (trust-safety incident queue) and TS-142 (outbox + relay) when the consumer subscription becomes feasible.
  - References: CLAUDE.md §12; PDD.md §16.1; TS-300; TS-142.

- [ ] **TS-065-followup-3** — Counter-party notification on dispute open + resolution

  - Acceptance: when `booking.dispute_opened` lands, `service-notification` sends a warmly-worded email/SMS to the counter-party (provider for family-filed disputes, family for provider-filed disputes, both for admin-filed). Sensitive categories (`welfare_concern`, `safety_concern`) are bracketed by ops triage before family notification (CLAUDE.md §12 family observability boundaries). On `booking.dispute_resolved`, send the outcome to both opener and counter-party. Lands alongside TS-073 (Postmark/SES + Twilio brought online) and TS-142.
  - References: PRD.md §6.4, §10.5; PDD.md §12.1; CLAUDE.md §12; TS-073; TS-142.

- [ ] **TS-065-followup-4** — Refund-policy application on `billing_dispute` resolutions

  - Acceptance: when `booking.dispute_resolved` lands with `outcome = 'resolved'` AND `reason = 'billing_dispute'`, the `service-accounting` consumer applies the refund-policy decision via TS-084 (refund + contra-revenue accounting work). The dispute row's resolution narrative drives the categorical refund amount (refund the booking commission portion, refund the full base price, issue goodwill credit, etc.). Lands with TS-084 + TS-142 when the consumer subscription becomes feasible.
  - References: PDD.md Appendix A; CLAUDE.md §6, §17.7; TS-084; TS-142.

The endpoints already exist behind `AccessTokenGuard`; TS-128 adds the UI + `@RequirePermissions('booking:adjust')` once `PermissionGuard` lifts (TS-052-followup-11). Tier-3 Concierge subscriptions trigger a `kind=concierge` thread per PRD §6.6. Idempotent on `event_id`. Lands alongside TS-142-followup-3 (the broader sweep that migrates HTTP scaffolds to relay subscriptions).

- [ ] **TS-071-followup-1** — OpenTelemetry tracing + Prometheus metrics for the realtime surface

  - Acceptance: incoming WebSocket handshakes produce OTel spans propagated through the membership lookup; `/metrics` exposes `realtime_connections_total{outcome=accepted|rejected,reason=missing_token|invalid_token|verify_error}`, `realtime_thread_joins_total{outcome=accepted|rejected,reason=not_a_participant|thread_archived|invalid_payload}`, `realtime_broadcasts_total{event}`, `realtime_active_sockets` (gauge sampled per pod). PII redacted at the logger and metric label level (userId never on metrics). Lands alongside `service-audit` (TS-100) where `@taste-and-see/tracing` gets its first real consumer. Mirrors TS-020-followup-1 / TS-072-followup-4 shape.
  - References: PDD.md §20.5; CLAUDE.md §10.

- [ ] **TS-071-followup-2** — Redis-backed per-user + per-IP rate limiting on handshakes + thread:join

  - Acceptance: a Redis sliding-window counter (mirror of the api-gateway's `RateLimitService` from TS-140) caps the number of new handshakes per source IP and the number of `thread:join` calls per user × per minute. Trip values default to 60 handshakes / 5 min per IP + 120 thread:join per user / 1 min. Hitting the cap returns a generic disconnect (handshake) / `{ok: false, error: 'rate_limited'}` ack (thread:join). Sibling to TS-025-followup-1's IP-level circuit breaker on /login. Lands once the `RateLimitService` package lifts out of api-gateway (TS-140-followup-x — currently captured in the gateway's app-local module).
  - References: PDD.md §11.1; CLAUDE.md §3.1.

- [ ] **TS-071-followup-3** — Migrate the synchronous handshake JWT verification to the TS-140-followup-1 trust-header envelope

  - Acceptance: when TS-140-followup-1a's per-service rollout lands service-messaging, the realtime handshake stops verifying the access-token JWT directly and instead consults the `x-ts-trust-*` headers signed by `api-gateway`. The gateway proxies the WebSocket upgrade (sticky-session-aware), signs the trust envelope, and the realtime gateway uses `TrustHeaderGuard` for the handshake instead of `verifyAccessToken`. Collapses the auth surface in line with the rest of the platform. Today the realtime gateway verifies JWTs directly because TS-071 ships ahead of the gateway-side WebSocket proxy.
  - References: PDD.md §7.3 + §13.1; TS-140-followup-1; TS-140-followup-1a.

- [ ] **TS-071-followup-4** — Testcontainers integration test: full handshake → thread:join → broadcast round-trip against real Postgres + Redis

  - Acceptance: `pnpm test:integration` (lands with TS-009e) boots Postgres + Redis (and a second app instance to validate cross-pod fan-out via the Redis adapter), applies the TS-070 migration, seeds a thread + a participant row, connects two `socket.io-client` sockets (one to each app instance), drives both through the `thread:join` handler, asserts `RealtimeBroadcaster.emitToThread(...)` delivers to both. Includes the negative paths: unauthenticated handshake disconnects, non-participant `thread:join` returns `not_a_participant`, archived thread returns `thread_archived`. Mirrors TS-070-followup-5 + TS-072-followup-5 shape.
  - References: PDD.md §24.1; CLAUDE.md §9.1; TS-009e.

- [ ] **TS-071-followup-5** — Observer-vs-member publish-time differentiation

  - Acceptance: when the future `message:send` handler (or the in-process producer pipeline TS-073-followup-4 plus the messages-svc HTTP write) emits a `message.created`, observers receive a slightly-different event payload than members (no draft-state, no "typing" indicator that another sibling task may add). Today the gateway treats members + observers identically — the read-only constraint isn't yet enforceable because there's no write surface. Captured here so the participant `role` field on `ThreadParticipant` ends up load-bearing for delivery shape.
  - References: CLAUDE.md §12 (family observability boundaries); PRD.md §6.4 + §6.7.

- [ ] **TS-071-followup-6** — Server-side `typing` + `read-receipt` events

  - Acceptance: two new closed-union events join `RealtimeEvent`: `typing.started` / `typing.stopped` (volatile — Socket.IO `volatile.emit` is the right shape) and `read-receipt.advanced` (durable; writes through to `thread_participants.last_read_message_id`). PRD.md §6.7 calls for read receipts (configurable); the wire format lands here, the per-thread configurability flag lands as a TS-070-followup. Volatile typing events ride on the existing room machinery; the read-receipt write goes through a small `MessagesReadCursorService` that updates the participant row inside a `$transaction`.
  - References: PRD.md §6.7.

- [ ] **TS-071-followup-7** — Lift the realtime guard + adapter scaffolding to `packages/nest-common` once a sibling service ships a WebSocket gateway

  - Acceptance: when the second service (likely `service-notification` for the in-app channel adapter from TS-073-followup-4) needs a Socket.IO gateway, the JWT-handshake auth + RedisIoAdapter scaffolding moves to `@taste-and-see/nest-common` alongside the AccessTokenGuard / ZodValidationPipe / RfcProblemFilter lift (TS-080-followup-2 / TS-072-followup-11). Mirrors the same "first consumer ships verbatim, second consumer triggers the lift" pattern the rest of the codebase uses.
  - References: TS-080-followup-2; TS-072-followup-11.

- [ ] **TS-071-followup-8** — Drop the `@WebSocketGateway` decorator's hardcoded `transports` slot once gateway-side proxying lands

  - Acceptance: the `transports: ['websocket', 'polling']` slot is set BOTH on the decorator (visible to Nest's gateway discovery) and on the IoAdapter's `createIOServer` options. Today the decorator's value is the fallback when a gateway is constructed without the adapter (e.g. in a future unit-test harness that drives Nest's gateway-bootstrap pipeline); the adapter's value is the production path. Drop the decorator-side default once we're confident every code path goes through the adapter.
  - References: `apps/service-messaging/src/realtime/realtime.gateway.ts` `@WebSocketGateway` decorator.

- [ ] **TS-073-followup-2** — Wire Twilio live SDK on the SmsDispatcher

  - Acceptance: when `TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID` / `TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN` / `NOTIFICATION_SMS_FROM_NUMBER` are all set, `SmsDispatcher.send` calls `new twilio(sid, token).messages.create({from, to, body})` and persists Twilio's `sid` as `providerMessageId`. Live mode kicks in only with all three values configured. Mirrors TS-073-followup-1 shape for stub-mode fall-back.
  - References: PDD.md §12.1; CLAUDE.md §13; `apps/service-notification/src/modules/dispatch/channels/sms-dispatcher.service.ts` "[live-pending]" branch.

- [ ] **TS-073-followup-3** — Wire firebase-admin live SDK on the PushDispatcher

  - Acceptance: when `FIREBASE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_B64` + `FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID` are set, `PushDispatcher.send` calls `admin.messaging().send({token, notification: {title, body}, ...})` and persists the FCM `messageId` as `providerMessageId`. The base64-encoded service account decodes to JSON at module-init time so the SDK initialises once. APNs delivery rides on the FCM-to-APNs proxy (PDD §12.1 covers both via `firebase-admin`).
  - References: PDD.md §12.1; CLAUDE.md §13; `apps/service-notification/src/modules/dispatch/channels/push-dispatcher.service.ts` "[live-pending]" branch.

  - Acceptance: every successful (or suppressed/failed) dispatch publishes a `notification.dispatched` event with the dispatch id, channel, category, status, suppressionReason / errorMessage. Consumers: `service-audit` (PDD §17.1 immutable log), `service-analytics` (per-channel delivery rate aggregates), the TS-072-followup-3 Cassandra cold-store keyspace. The outbox append must run inside the same Prisma `$transaction` as the dispatch row write — today the orchestrator writes directly without a transaction since there's no co-mutating side effect. Lands alongside TS-142 (outbox + relay infrastructure).

The relay consumer in service-notification picks the event up and calls `DispatchOrchestratorService.dispatch` in-process. The HTTP scaffold stays for manual ops re-dispatch + admin tooling but becomes the secondary surface. Mirrors TS-081-followup-2 / TS-082-followup-1 shape.
  - References: PDD.md §7.3; CLAUDE.md §5.3; TS-142.

Every successful `DispatchOrchestratorService.dispatch` also writes the per-user delivery row to Cassandra (best-effort — Cassandra write failures log + alert but don't fail the dispatch). Adds `/readyz` `cassandra: 'ok'` check additively. Supersedes TS-072-followup-3 which was named at TS-072 landing time.
  - References: PDD.md §8.3, §13.1; CLAUDE.md §4.2; TS-072-followup-3.

- [ ] **TS-073-followup-8** — BullMQ retry-on-failure worker for transient channel errors

  - Acceptance: when a channel adapter returns `failed` with a transient-error indicator (Postmark 5xx, Twilio rate-limit, FCM unavailable), the orchestrator enqueues a BullMQ retry job with exponential backoff + jitter (max 5 attempts over ~10 min). Permanent errors (Postmark 422 invalid recipient, Twilio invalid number, FCM unregistered token) skip the retry and stay as `failed`. Lands once BullMQ cross-cutting workers infra is wired (TS-142 outbox / cross-cutting workers).
  - References: PDD.md §12.1 deliverability; CLAUDE.md §5.2 retries; TS-142.

- [ ] **TS-073-followup-10** — Testcontainers integration test: full dispatch round-trip against a real Postgres

  - Acceptance: `pnpm test:integration` (lands with TS-009e) exercises the full HTTP flow with a live Postgres. (1) Apply the TS-072 + TS-073 migrations → seed a template + active version → POST /api/v1/internal/notification/dispatch with the shared-secret header → SELECT the dispatch row to assert status=sent + providerMessageId stub-prefix + the CHECK constraint enforces per-status invariants at the DB layer. (2) Replay the same `idempotencyKey` → assert the response is the original row with `replayed: true` and DB row count is still 1. (3) Toggle preference opt-out → POST → assert status=suppressed_by_preference + suppressionReason persisted. (4) Configure quiet-hours window + POST inside-window → assert suppressed_by_quiet_hours. (5) POST `bypassQuietHours=true` for transactional → assert sent. (6) GET /api/v1/admin/notification/dispatches with a valid bearer token → assert pagination + filters round-trip. Catches drift between the FakePrisma `$transaction` semantics and Postgres' CHECK + UNIQUE behaviour. Mirrors TS-072-followup-5 shape.
  - References: PDD.md §24.1; CLAUDE.md §9.1; TS-009e.

PDF kinds bypass Sharp and write the original bytes to the delivery key. `Sharp({ limitInputPixels: 24_000_000 })` is the hard floor — CLAUDE.md §17.15 absolute prohibition. - [ ] **TS-111-followup-4-followup-1** — Logical child spans + the actor/tenant frame on the search trace

  - Acceptance: the auto-instrumentation gives service-search the inbound HTTP server span + the outbound sponsored-resolve client span for free, but the in-process backend query / ranking / sponsored-overlay steps are NOT broken out as child spans, so a slow Phase-1 in-memory scan (or, post-TS-111-followup-1, a slow ES query vs. a slow sponsored hop) can't be told apart on the trace. Wrap `ProviderSearchService.search`'s backend call + the `overlaySponsoredSlots` step in `withSpan(...)` (from `@taste-and-see/tracing`) child spans, and stamp the actor/tenant scope (already seeded on `request.requestContext` by `AccessTokenGuard` + `TenantContextInterceptor`) as span attributes — keeping PII off the attributes (userId is an opaque id, never email/name). Lands once a real latency-tail investigation needs the per-step breakdown; today the counters + the two auto spans cover the budget alerting.
  - References: CLAUDE.md §10; PDD.md §20.5; `apps/service-search/src/modules/providers/services/provider-search.service.ts`; TS-111-followup-4.

  - Acceptance: `POST /api/v1/search/providers` adds `@RequirePermissions('provider:search')` once the shared `PermissionGuard` / `@RequirePermissions` decorator lift from `service-provider`'s `common/` lands (TS-052-followup-11). Today the surface authenticates via JWT but does not gate on a specific permission — every authenticated user can search. - [ ] **TS-111-followup-7** — Idempotency cache on the internal upsert / delete surface

  - Acceptance: `PUT|DELETE /api/v1/internal/search/providers/:providerId` accepts an `Idempotency-Key` header and replays a stored response on a duplicate retry from the indexer. Lands with `@taste-and-see/nest-idempotency`'s Redis-backed mode (TS-044 introduced the package). Today the backend's `sourceUpdatedAt`-based dedup is the practical idempotency mechanism — but a network retry that lands AFTER a fresher event has been processed would still get a 200 from the backend with `outcome=unchanged`, which is the correct outcome but obscures the actual operation that ran. The cache surfaces the exact original response.
  - References: CLAUDE.md §3.3; `packages/nest-idempotency`; TS-044.

- [ ] **TS-111-followup-8** — Drop the in-memory `offset:N` cursor for HMAC-sealed cursor tokens

  - Acceptance: `parseOffsetCursor` / nextCursor minting moves to an HMAC-sealed format encoding `(offset, generation, filterHash)` so an adversarial client can't supply an arbitrary offset to bypass paging caps or skip the filter check. Today the `offset:N` shape is harmless (no row-level access yet — TS-141-followup-3 — so an attacker can't escalate by jumping offsets within the same query). Captured up-front so the cursor format has a named upgrade path.
  - References: CLAUDE.md §3.2.

- [ ] **TS-111-followup-9** — Honour partner-tenant scoping once TS-141-followup-3 lands

  - Acceptance: `ProviderSearchService.search` filters results by the caller's tenant scope when the access-token carries a `tenantScope: { type: 'tenant', tenantId }` frame. Phase-1 search ignores tenant scope entirely — every authenticated user can see every active provider. Once TS-141-followup-3 ships the per-model row-level filter helpers, the indexed `ProviderDiscoveryDocument` gains a `tenantIds[]` field and the search backend filters at query time. Captured up-front so the tenant-scoping has a named owner.
  - References: CLAUDE.md §3.2; PDD.md §10.2; TS-141-followup-3.
