- [ ] **TS-124-followup-1** — Wire household-svc resolution into the checkout customerId

  - Acceptance: the family-portal `checkout-form` reads the user's household id from `household-svc` (via the gateway) rather than passing the user's `userId` as the soft FK `customerId`. Today the action passes `customerId: me.userId` as a documented Phase-1 simplification (the JWT carries the userId, the household-svc cross-service lookup that would translate it to a `households.id` is deferred). Once household-svc grows a `GET /api/v1/households/me` (or the gateway aggregates it into `/me`), the form gets the actual household id and the FK semantics in subscriptions.customer_id match `households.id` end-to-end.
  - References: `apps/web-family/app/(protected)/checkout/[planCode]/page.tsx` `me.userId` comment; PRD.md §6.1; PDD.md §8.2 (households).

- [ ] **TS-124-followup-2** — Surface the user's email on `GET /api/v1/me` so the checkout form can pre-fill it

  - Acceptance: service-identity's `TokenService.signAccessToken` includes `email` as a JWT claim; the auth-sdk `RequestContext` carries it; `gateway-me.schema.ts` `MeResponse` grows an `email` field; the family-portal's `/checkout/[planCode]/page.tsx` pre-fills the form (instead of asking the user to re-enter it). Today the checkout form re-collects the email because `/me` is JWT-derived and the JWT does not carry `email`. Modest contracts change + a service-identity migration — not strictly a security concern (email is already in service-identity's `users` table) but a UX cleanup that crosses the contracts boundary.
  - References: `apps/web-family/app/(protected)/checkout/[planCode]/actions.ts` doc-comment; CLAUDE.md §3.1; `packages/contracts/src/http/gateway-me.schema.ts`.

- [ ] **TS-124-followup-3** — Auto-resolve the user's active subscription id on `/billing/invoices`

  - Acceptance: the page accepts an empty `subscriptionId` query and falls back to calling a future `GET /api/v1/subscriptions?customerId=...` endpoint to pick the active subscription. Today the invoices page renders an explainer when `?subscriptionId=` is missing because we don't yet have a `GET /subscriptions` list endpoint. Lands when the subscriptions list surface exists (TS-127 admin tooling delivers it for admin scope; the customer-scoped equivalent can come from the same module).
  - References: `apps/web-family/app/(protected)/billing/invoices/page.tsx` `Empty` placeholder; PRD.md §6.2.

- [ ] **TS-124-followup-4** — Stripe Checkout webhook handler that finalizes server-side on `checkout.session.completed`

  - Acceptance: the inbound `service-webhook` stripe ingress relays `checkout.session.completed` events into `service-subscription` via the outbox (TS-145 outbox consumer wiring), and the relay calls `CheckoutSessionsService.finalize` server-side so the local subscription row exists even when the customer closes the browser tab before reaching `/checkout/success`. The current implementation relies on the success-page hit to trigger finalize; an abandoned-tab race leaves the row missing until the customer re-visits. Defensive backstop, captured up-front so the gap has a named owner.
  - References: PDD.md §7.3 outbox pattern; `apps/service-webhook/src/modules/stripe/services/stripe-ingress.service.ts` doc-comment.

- [ ] **TS-124-followup-5** — Persist coupon redemption at finalize time (not at session-create)

  - Acceptance: when a Stripe Checkout Session is created with a coupon, the `coupon_redemptions` row is currently NOT persisted on our side (the Stripe-side discount is applied during the hosted flow, but the local `coupon_redemptions.subscription_id` link is never set because the local subscription row doesn't exist yet). At finalize time, the service should re-read `validatedCoupon` and call `CouponsService.recordRedemption` inside the same transaction as the subscription row insert. Captured because the create-flow path of `SubscriptionsService` already does this — the divergence between the two creation paths is a known gap.
  - References: `apps/service-subscription/src/modules/checkout/services/checkout-sessions.service.ts` `finalize` comment; `apps/service-subscription/src/modules/subscriptions/services/subscriptions.service.ts` coupon-redemption logic.

- [ ] **TS-124-followup-6** — Forward inbound `Idempotency-Key` from gateway to service-subscription on the checkout proxies

  - Acceptance: the gateway proxies for POST `/checkout-sessions` and POST `/checkout-sessions/:id/finalize` carry an Idempotency-Key on the outbound fetch when the inbound caller supplied one. Today the gateway's `DownstreamCallOptions` does not allow-list `Idempotency-Key` in its outbound headers, so the service-subscription `@Idempotent()` decorator sees no key on the gateway-issued retry. Service-subscription still produces a same-output for the same input (the underlying Stripe call is idempotent on its own keys), but a gateway-level cache hit would beat the downstream call. Lands alongside TS-140-followup-5 (gateway-side idempotency cache).
  - References: `apps/api-gateway/src/modules/gateway-routes/auth-proxy.controller.ts` Idempotency-Key gap comment; TS-140-followup-5.

Lands with TS-009e Testcontainers infra so the gateway + service-subscription + postgres + redis spin up reliably under CI. Today the unit + contract layers cover the typed contracts; the E2E covers the cookie round-trip + redirect-flow + post-Stripe-return semantics.
  - References: PDD.md §24.1; CLAUDE.md §9.1; TS-009e.

Mirrors TS-020-followup-1 / TS-140-followup-4. Lands once `@taste-and-see/tracing` is wired into the cross-service exporter chain.

- [ ] **TS-126-followup-1a** — Restore from `deactivated` via a dedicated endpoint

  - Acceptance: a separate `POST /api/v1/admin/users/:id/restore` surface (NOT reinstate — the semantics differ) accepts a request to bring a deactivated account back. Today `reinstate` rejects `deactivated → active` with `illegal_transition` to keep the lifecycle invariant clean (deactivated is the permanent-close terminus). Restoring requires a separate permission + a deliberate ops decision; the surface should require both a reason and an explicit "I confirm this account was deactivated in error" acknowledgement. Lands when product justifies the case.
  - References: PRD.md §10.2; `apps/service-identity/src/modules/admin/services/admin-user-actions.service.ts` `reinstate` doc-comment.

The mint endpoint, `actorOnBehalfOf` claim, short-TTL session (`IMPERSONATION_SESSION_TTL_SECONDS`), start/end audit events, and web-admin diagnostic banner all exist since TS-297 — this task is ONLY the cross-origin portal experience. - [ ] **TS-127-followup-1** — Admin: manual subscription overrides (comp / refund / extend-trial / prorate)

  - Acceptance: `POST /api/v1/admin/subscriptions/:id/comp` (issue a goodwill credit + extend the period without charging), `POST /api/v1/admin/subscriptions/:id/refund` (refund the most-recent invoice or a specific one), `POST /api/v1/admin/subscriptions/:id/extend-trial` (push `trialEnd` forward), `POST /api/v1/admin/subscriptions/:id/prorate` (mid-period plan change with proration). All four require `super_admin` (or finer permissions once TS-127-followup-10 lifts the gate); all four emit an audit event (TS-127-followup-6) with before/after diff; all four `@Idempotent()`. Web-admin `/subscriptions/[id]` Actions section grows the four buttons with destructive-confirm modals where appropriate.
  - References: PRD.md §10.3 "Manual subscription overrides: comp, extend trial, refund, prorate"; CLAUDE.md §3.2, §3.6; TS-084 (refund + contra-revenue accounting); TS-127.

- [ ] **TS-127-followup-2** — Admin: plan catalog management (create / edit / archive)

  - Acceptance: `POST /api/v1/admin/plans` (create), `PATCH /api/v1/admin/plans/:id` (edit name / description / features / sortPosition / active — never `code` / `customerGroup` / pricing once subscriptions reference it), `DELETE /api/v1/admin/plans/:id` (flips `active=false` — never a hard delete, every historical subscription must keep pointing at a valid plan row). All gated by `super_admin` + `@Idempotent()`; pricing-change edits require a fresh `code` (immutable cross-system identifier — `subscription.activated.planCode` event payload + invoice line item descriptions depend on it). Web-admin `/plans` list + detail editor surfaces; emits `plan.catalog_updated` via the outbox (TS-040-followup-5) once that arrives.
  - References: PRD.md §10.3 "Plan catalog (create, edit, archive plans)"; PRD.md §5; PDD.md §11.1; TS-040-followup-5; TS-127.

- [ ] **TS-127-followup-3** — Admin: bulk operations (cohort grants, status sweeps)

  - Acceptance: `POST /api/v1/admin/subscriptions/bulk/extend-grace` (grant 30-day grace extension to every past-due subscription matching a filter — by plan, customer-group, or signup-cohort), `POST /api/v1/admin/subscriptions/bulk/comp` (free month grant to a cohort), `POST /api/v1/admin/subscriptions/bulk/cancel` (mass cancel for a partner termination). Each accepts a structured filter + reason code + actor; each runs as a BullMQ job with progress reporting + a one-shot admin review surface before mutations land. Mandatory dry-run mode shows the affected row count before commit. Web-admin grows a `/subscriptions/bulk` page guarded by an extra-strict CSRF token + the standard super_admin gate.
  - References: PRD.md §10.3 "Bulk operations (e.g., grant 30-day extension to a cohort)"; CLAUDE.md §3.2; TS-127.

- [ ] **TS-127-followup-4** — Revenue recognition reporting (deferred → recognized cohort view)

  - Acceptance: cross-service admin tooling that aggregates `accounting.deferred_revenue_balances` (TS-082) by subscription cohort + plan + month so finance can answer "how much revenue is deferred vs recognized as of today across active subscriptions?". New `GET /api/v1/admin/subscriptions/revenue-recognition?period=2026-05` proxied through the gateway to a new service-accounting endpoint that joins the deferred-balance + recognition-event tables. Web-admin `/subscriptions/revenue-recognition` page renders a per-plan summary + drill-down per subscription. Read-only — every adjustment goes through the existing service-accounting period-close / journal flow.
  - References: PRD.md §10.3 "Revenue recognition reporting (deferred → recognized)"; PDD.md §11.2; CLAUDE.md §6; TS-082; TS-127.

- [ ] **TS-127-followup-5** — Manual dunning recovery actions (retry now, mark recovered, force exhausted)

  - Acceptance: `POST /api/v1/admin/subscriptions/:id/dunning/retry-now` (force-immediate Stripe collection attempt outside the smart-retry cadence), `POST /api/v1/admin/subscriptions/:id/dunning/mark-recovered` (manually record a successful out-of-band payment — wires through to `DunningService.recordPaymentSuccess`), `POST /api/v1/admin/subscriptions/:id/dunning/force-exhausted` (skip the grace window — flips status to `unpaid` immediately). All gated by `super_admin` + `@Idempotent()`. Sibling to TS-042-followup-5 which captures the same surface from the dunning-side; this follow-up wires it into the admin-tooling UX.
  - References: PRD.md §10.3 "Dunning management"; PRD.md §10.3 "Dunning view"; TS-042-followup-5; TS-127.

- [ ] **TS-140-followup-1a-1** — Drop the bearer path per service once TS-151 NetworkPolicy cordons downstream routes

  - `AccessTokenGuard` now accepts either a gateway trust envelope or a bearer JWT. The bearer half exists only
    because downstream service routes are still reachable in-cluster by direct callers; it is the weaker of the
    two and the original TS-140-followup-1 design says so. Once TS-151 restricts those routes to the gateway,
    each service can move to `TrustHeaderGuard` (trust-only) and the JWT verification secret can leave that
    service's environment entirely — which is the real prize: today every service holds `JWT_ACCESS_SECRET`, the
    HS256 signing key, and any one of them could mint tokens for the whole platform.
  - Do it per service, and only after TS-151 — a service cordoned in staging but not in production would 401
    every direct caller with no way back except a redeploy.
  - Acceptance: for each cordoned service, routes carry `TrustHeaderGuard`, `NestAuthModule.forRoot` drops
    `jwtAccessSecret`, and `JWT_ACCESS_SECRET` is removed from its Secret.
  - References: `packages/nest-internal-trust/`; TS-151; CLAUDE.md §3.1, §3.2.

- [ ] **TS-140-followup-1a-2** — RFC 7807 extension members are still being dropped, four features' worth

  - TS-510 found `RfcProblemFilter` silently dropping `code` and `issues`, and fixed those two by name. The
    allow-list is now `errors` / `code` / `issues` — so **every other extension member a controller attaches is
    still discarded**. Confirmed live during TS-505c: service-booking's tier-gating refusal attaches
    `violationReason` / `householdTier` / `providerTier`, its illegal-transition 409 attaches
    `allowedTransitions`, its accept-window 409 attaches `windowExpiredAt`, and its hold refusal attaches
    `incidentId` — a client sees none of them. The E2E spec therefore has to assert on English prose in `detail`,
    which is the exact failure mode the `code` fix was written to end.
  - The question is not "add four more names" — it is where the allow-list should live. A member attached by a
    controller and dropped by a global filter is invisible at every layer: the controller compiles, the unit test
    asserts the thrown body, and only the wire disagrees. Candidate shape: extension members declared on the
    problem-body type the controller throws, so the filter allow-lists by construction and an undeclared member
    is a compile error rather than a silent drop.
  - **Never a spread** — the filter's own doc-block explains why (an exception body accumulates internal detail).
  - Acceptance: a controller that attaches an extension member either reaches the client with it or fails to
    compile; the six members named above reach the client; a test asserts an *un*declared member is still dropped.
  - References: `packages/nest-common/src/rfc-problem.filter.ts`; TS-510; CLAUDE.md §5.1.

- [ ] **TS-140-followup-5** — Idempotency cache on write proxies

  - Acceptance: when the gateway grows POST / PATCH / DELETE proxy paths (TS-124 subscription checkout proxy, TS-125 booking creation proxy), each one is decorated with `@Idempotent()` from `@taste-and-see/nest-idempotency` (TS-044) so a client-side retry hits the cached response without re-hitting the downstream. Today the gateway is read-only (only GET /me + GET /plans); the wiring lands when the first write-path proxy materialises. Captured up-front so the future proxies have a named integration point.
  - **STILL OPEN, and the completed-side claim is a DIFFERENT mechanism (checked 2026-07-28).** TS-140's entry says it "closes TS-140-followup-5 / TS-125-followup-10 **for the proxies that adopt it**" — what shipped is `DownstreamHttpClient` FORWARDING an inbound `Idempotency-Key` header verbatim to the downstream service, so the downstream's own `@Idempotent()` collapses the retry. This entry asks for something else: `@Idempotent()` on the GATEWAY handler, so the gateway caches and replays its own response.
  - **Decide whether that is even wanted before building it.** Forwarding means ONE cache, owned by the service that owns the write; adding a second at the gateway means two caches with independent TTLs that can disagree about what the first response was, and the gateway's copy would shadow a downstream that had since changed its mind. The honest options are (a) close this as superseded by forwarding, (b) apply `@Idempotent()` only to gateway routes that AGGREGATE (where the gateway composes a response no single downstream owns). (b) is the defensible one; (a) is probably right for every pure pass-through proxy.
  - References: CLAUDE.md §3.3; `packages/nest-idempotency/`; TS-044; TS-140.

Captured here so the seeds get audited before the enforce flip.

- [ ] **TS-142-followup-5** — Dead-letter admin surface

  - Acceptance: `GET /api/v1/admin/outbox/dead-lettered` lists every row whose `attempts >= MAX_ATTEMPTS` AND `dispatched_at IS NULL`, paginated by source. `POST /api/v1/admin/outbox/:source/:eventId/redispatch` resets `attempts` to 0 + clears `last_error` so the relay re-picks the row next cycle. Both behind `super_admin` + MFA. Lives in the relay (or in a small admin-tooling sidecar) since it owns the operational view of the outbox; the producer services have no read path into their own outbox by design (PDD §7.3 — outbox is a relay implementation detail, not a service surface). Lands alongside TS-126 admin tooling.
  - References: PRD.md §10.2, §10.13; CLAUDE.md §3.2; TS-126.

- [ ] **TS-142-followup-6** — Outbox row janitor / pruning worker

  - Acceptance: a BullMQ scheduled worker prunes every service's `{schema}.outbox_events WHERE dispatched_at < now() - retention_window` (default: 30 days — enough to support replay during incident response without unbounded growth). Configurable per environment. Dead-lettered rows are intentionally preserved indefinitely (their existence is the audit trail of unresolved producer→bus drift). Lands once BullMQ infra is wired (TS-022-followup-3 shape).
  - References: CLAUDE.md §4.1, §4.3; `apps/service-subscription/prisma/schema.prisma` `OutboxEvent` doc-comment.

- [ ] **TS-142-followup-7** — Testcontainers integration test: full TS-142 round-trip against real Postgres + Redis

  - Acceptance: `pnpm test:integration` (lands with TS-009e) boots Postgres + Redis containers, applies the service-subscription init migration + the TS-142 migration, runs the SDK + relay in-process, and exercises the full flow: insert an event via `OutboxService.append` inside a transaction → assert the row lands in Postgres with `dispatched_at IS NULL` → run `RelayWorkerService.pollOnce` → assert `dispatched_at` is stamped + the Redis stream `events:subscription.activated` carries the entry with the expected key-value pairs. Validates that the SDK's raw-SQL template surface plays correctly with real Prisma + that the relay's `pg`-backed queries match Postgres' actual unique-constraint + partial-index semantics. Mirrors TS-026-followup-6 / TS-041b-followup-6 / TS-051-followup-6 shape.
  - References: PDD.md §24.1; CLAUDE.md §9.1; TS-009e.

- [ ] **TS-142-followup-8** — Multi-replica relay with `SELECT … FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`

  - Acceptance: when Phase 2 brings event volume that one replica can't sustain, the `PgOutboxClaimRepository.claimBatch` query adds `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` so multiple relay replicas can poll the same source without dispatching the same row twice. Lands when the per-source dispatch rate exceeds ~500 events/s (the rough single-replica limit at the default poll interval + batch size). Today the single-replica posture is correct and observable; the lock clause is a deliberate forward-compatibility deferral.
  - References: `apps/workers/outbox-relay/src/relay/outbox-claim.repository.ts` `claimBatch` doc-comment; PDD.md §29.1 (Phase 3 Kafka migration is the other scale lever).

- [ ] **TS-150-followup-1** — Scaffold `env/staging/` and `env/prod/` env roots

  - Acceptance: `infra/terraform/env/staging/` and `infra/terraform/env/prod/` mirror the dev shape (`versions.tf` + `providers.tf` + `backend.tf` + `variables.tf` + `main.tf` + `outputs.tf` + `terraform.tfvars.example`). Each consumes the same `modules/*` tree; per-env sizing diverges only via tfvars (staging: 3× Cloud VPS M + 1× Cloud VPS L data node; prod: 3× Cloud VPS L + 1× Cloud VPS XL data node + 2 TB object storage). New Terraform Cloud workspaces `tastesee-staging` and `tastesee-prod`. Lands once dev is proven on a first apply against real Contabo credentials.
  - References: PDD.md §20.3; `infra/terraform/README.md`; ADR-0001.

- [ ] **TS-150-followup-2** — Streaming Postgres replica + automatic failover on the data tier

  - Acceptance: a second Contabo Cloud VPS L joins the private VLAN as a streaming standby; `pgBackRest`'s `repo1-host` + the standby's `primary_conninfo` are templated by Terraform; `patroni` (or `pg_auto_failover`) drives leader election. The data-node module grows a `replica_count` variable (default 0 in dev, 1 in prod). RPO drops to ~0 on the streaming path while pgBackRest remains the cold-backup floor. Lands once dev validates the single-node path.
  - References: PDD.md §20.6; `infra/terraform/modules/data-node/` doc-comment on the Phase-1 single-node posture.

- [ ] **TS-150-followup-3** — Off-provider backup mirror (Backblaze B2) for prod

  - Acceptance: `pgBackRest` adds a second repo (`repo2-type=s3`) pointed at a Backblaze B2 bucket; `bandwidth_limit` configured so the off-provider mirror doesn't starve the primary backup path; lifecycle rules retain 30 d on B2 (1.5× Contabo retention) to insulate against a Contabo-side compromise. New Terraform Backblaze provider config in `env/prod/`. Lands with prod env (TS-150-followup-1).
  - References: PDD.md §20.6 ("off-provider mirror to a separate S3-compatible bucket for the prod env").

- [ ] **TS-150-followup-4** — keepalived (or BGP) for ingress-node failover

  - Acceptance: NGINX Ingress runs as a DaemonSet on two of the three cluster nodes with `hostPort: 443`; a shared VIP fronts both via `keepalived` (active/passive) or a Contabo floating IP (when available); Cloudflare A records resolve to the VIP instead of each node IP. Removes the single-node failure mode that currently requires a DNS flip. Deferred until uptime telemetry shows the DNS-flip path costs > 1 min of edge availability per incident.
  - References: `infra/terraform/README.md` § Known caveats; PDD.md §20.6.

Cluster manifests + Helm releases + ArgoCD apps move 1:1 (ADR-0001 §"Preserved (no regression)"). Captured here so the migration has a named owner; trigger conditions in ADR-0001 §"Phase 3 migration trigger".
  - References: ADR-0001; PDD.md §16.4, §20.2; TS-410.

  - Acceptance: a documented, applied configuration for running Postgres 16 + Redis 7 on the same box as k3s — the `ExternalName` patch targets AND the egress-NetworkPolicy `ipBlock` widened to reach them. `base/data-access/egress-network-policies.yaml` permits `10.40.0.0/24` on 5432/6379 only, and every namespace is default-deny, so a host-local datastore outside that CIDR leaves every pod healthy on its probes and unable to run a single query. Ideally ships as an opt-in component (mirroring `components/single-node`) rather than as runbook prose, since prose is what gets skipped. Also needs the 20 per-service databases + roles created, since CLAUDE.md §2.3 forbids sharing a schema across bounded contexts.

- [ ] **TS-009-followup-1** — ESLint lints ZERO TypeScript in this repository

  - Acceptance: `@typescript-eslint/parser` (and the plugin, for the rules that need type information) wired into `packages/eslint-config/base.cjs`; every package's `lint` script gains `--ext .ts,.tsx` (or moves to flat config, which infers extensions); `turbo run lint` demonstrably lints the ~3,000 TypeScript sources rather than 34 `.eslintrc.cjs` files; the resulting violations fixed or explicitly ruled-off with rationale.
  - **Evidence, measured 2026-08-07.** Two independent defects compound into total blindness: (1) `base.cjs` sets `parserOptions` but no `parser`, so ESLint uses espree and every `.ts` file fails with `Parsing error: Unexpected token` — reproduced from both the repo root and inside the package, so it is not config resolution; (2) each package's lint script is `eslint .` with no `--ext`, and **ESLint 8 lints only `.js` by default when given a directory**, so the parse errors are never triggered. Measured in `apps/service-webhook`: `eslint .` reports **1 file linted — its own `.eslintrc.cjs` — against 40 TypeScript sources**. `turbo run lint` has been green for the entire life of the project because it examines no TypeScript.
  - **Why this matters beyond hygiene:** `base.cjs` exists largely to enforce CLAUDE.md §3.9 banned patterns — `no-eval`, `no-implied-eval`, `no-new-func`, and `no-empty` with `allowEmptyCatch: false` (§3.9's "no silent error swallowing"). None of those has ever been evaluated against a single `.ts` file. §2.4 states lint is a pre-commit gate; it is not one.
  - Sizing: a probe with a proper parser over `apps/service-webhook` linted all 40 files with **zero real violations** (the one reported error was a phantom — an inline `eslint-disable` naming a rule that was not loaded). That suggests the fix is cheap, but it is one package of 34 and must not be treated as a whole-workspace measurement. Expect `no-console` warnings to be the common case, and note `--max-warnings=0` makes warnings fatal.
  - Discovered while unblocking the initial commit: the pre-commit hook failed on 23 parse errors. `lint-staged.config.cjs` was narrowed to `.js`-family files so the hook is honest rather than broken; that narrowing is the thing this task reverts.
  - References: `packages/eslint-config/base.cjs`; `lint-staged.config.cjs`; `.husky/pre-commit`; CLAUDE.md §2.4, §3.9.

- [ ] **TS-151-followup-16** — Reconcile the `api.<env>` DNS record with the api-gateway's lack of an Ingress

  - Acceptance: either (a) the Terraform `dns` module stops creating an `api` A record, or (b) the api-gateway gains an Ingress and a documented reason for exposing it. Today the record is created and **nothing serves it** — `kubectl kustomize infra/kubernetes/services/api-gateway` emits zero Ingress objects, and requests to `api.<env>.tasteseelife.com` land on the ingress controller's default backend. (a) is the likely answer: all four portals reach the gateway at `http://api-gateway.platform-services.svc.cluster.local:3000` and no `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` variable exposes a gateway URL, so the browser never talks to it — the BFF boundary is server-side by design. Decide before a public API, a mobile client, or the deferred browser-WebSocket surface (TS-071 / TS-140-followup-1a) makes a public gateway hostname genuinely necessary, because at that point the answer changes and the CORS/cookie posture has to be revisited with it.
  - References: `infra/terraform/modules/dns/main.tf` (lines 9–11); `infra/kubernetes/services/api-gateway/kustomization.yaml`; `docs/deployment/vps-runbook.md` § 1.1.

  - **Do not bundle this with an unrelated change.** The remedy is mechanical (`pnpm -F @taste-and-see/contracts generate:openapi`), but a 15k-line artifact diff needs its own commit and its own review — the whole point of the gate is that a schema change reaches downstream consumers deliberately. - [ ] **TS-152-followup-1** — Promote ArgoCD to HA (3× controllers / 3× server / Redis sentinel)

  - Acceptance: `install/values.yaml` flips `controller.replicas` / `server.replicas` / `repoServer.replicas` from 1 → 3 + enables the bundled Redis sentinel + adds PDBs on each. Pairs with TS-151-followup-6 (observability stack — having three replicas without metrics is half a win). Gated on cluster growth past the Phase-1 baseline (3× Cloud VPS L); today an outage of an ArgoCD controller pauses CD but does NOT affect running workloads, so single-replica is operationally acceptable.
  - References: `infra/argocd/install/values.yaml`; PDD.md §20.2; ADR-0001.

- [ ] **TS-152-followup-2** — SSO via Dex + per-team RBAC + public ingress for the ArgoCD UI

  - Acceptance: `install/values.yaml` flips `dex.enabled: true`, wires OIDC against the company IdP (GitHub OAuth / Google Workspace / Okta — pick once IdP is chosen), enables `server.ingress.enabled` with `cert-manager.io/cluster-issuer: letsencrypt-prod`, and replaces the placeholder `argocd.invalid.local` domain with a real hostname (`argocd.tasteseelife.com`). RBAC policy expands from the local-admin-only Phase-1 shape to per-team grants (`role:ops`, `role:finance`, `role:trust-safety` matching the PDD §10 admin role split). Until then operators reach the UI via `kubectl port-forward`.
  - References: `infra/argocd/install/values.yaml` (configs.cm.admin.enabled + configs.rbac.policy.csv); PDD.md §10.12; CLAUDE.md §3.1.

- [ ] **TS-152-followup-3** — Tighten ArgoCD namespace PSS from `baseline` to `restricted`

  - Acceptance: `install/namespace.yaml` flips `pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce: baseline` → `restricted` once the upstream argo-cd chart's repo-server / dex pods satisfy the restricted bar (non-root, no privileged caps, readOnlyRootFilesystem, seccompProfile=RuntimeDefault). Today the repo-server needs `git`/`helm` binaries + a writable working directory that the chart's defaults don't compose into a restricted-PSS-clean shape. Track upstream chart progress; flip when chart values can satisfy the bar (or land a sidecar wrapper that does). Mirrors TS-151-followup-3 shape.
  - References: `infra/argocd/install/namespace.yaml`; PDD.md §20.2; CLAUDE.md §17.

- [ ] **TS-152-followup-4** — ApplicationSet for per-service / per-overlay scaling

  - Acceptance: when the per-service split becomes operationally meaningful (per-service sync windows, per-service health gates, Argo Rollouts canary controllers — typically when the second / third service ships its per-service Kustomize base via TS-151-followup-1), `infra/argocd/applications/{env}/` is replaced by an `ApplicationSet` manifest whose Generator iterates over `infra/kubernetes/services/*/` and emits one Application per service per env. The current single-Application-per-env shape is structurally compatible: the ApplicationSet's `template.spec` matches the existing platform.yaml shape exactly. Lands incrementally as each new service base proves the pattern.
  - References: `infra/argocd/applications/dev/platform.yaml` doc-comment; PDD.md §20.4.

Templates land for the load-bearing transitions: `on-sync-failed`, `on-health-degraded`, `on-sync-succeeded` (prod only — staging is too noisy to alert on). Per-Application subscriptions stamp `notifications.argoproj.io/subscribe.on-sync-failed.slack: ops-deploys` annotations on the child Applications. Until then the notifications controller is installed but silent.
  - References: `infra/argocd/install/values.yaml` `notifications.enabled`; PDD.md §12.1, §20.5; CLAUDE.md §10.

- [ ] **TS-152-followup-6** — Signed-commit gate via cosign + `signatureKeys` on the prod AppProject

  - Acceptance: prod `argocd app sync` rejects a commit whose tip is not signed by an allow-listed cosign key. `platform-prod.yaml` adds a `signatureKeys` array referencing the public key fingerprints; the operator's commit-signing setup uses cosign keyless signing (Sigstore / Fulcio). Closes the "operator-discretion-only" gap on the prod promotion gate — today the AppProject's syncWindows + manual sync require operator intent, but nothing on-chain prevents a compromised git server from substituting commits. Gated on a cosign rollout for the Phase-1 ops team.
  - References: `infra/argocd/projects/platform-prod.yaml` `syncPolicy` doc-comment; CLAUDE.md §11, §17.12; ADR-0001 §"Phase 3 migration trigger".

  - Acceptance: a sibling install overlay (`infra/argo-rollouts/install/`) Helm-inflates the argo-rollouts chart. Per-service overlays for booking / accounting / payouts swap `Deployment` for `Rollout` with a canary strategy (10% → 50% → 100% with a 5m bake at each step + automated `analysis.template` health checks against the service's `/metrics` endpoint). The reusable `nestjs-service` component grows a `strategy: Canary` switch behind a Kustomize patch; existing Deployments remain unchanged. Lands when the first high-risk service (likely service-booking or service-accounting) needs canary semantics in prod.
  - References: PDD.md §20.4 "Progressive delivery via Argo Rollouts (canary or blue/green) for high-risk services"; CLAUDE.md §11.

Until then the repo URL in every Application + AppProject `sourceRepos` must remain public-readable. Pairs with the sealed-secrets / external-secrets wiring (TS-151-followup-2) — both rely on the same Secret-management pattern.
  - References: `infra/argocd/README.md` § "Phase 1 caveats"; TS-151-followup-2.

Mirrors TS-151-followup-9 shape (kubernetes/ tree's lint gate).
  - References: `infra/argocd/README.md` § "CI gates (deferred)"; CLAUDE.md §11.

  - Acceptance: an operator with kubeconfig access runs the three-step bootstrap against the real Contabo k3s cluster (once TS-150-followup-6 and TS-151-followup-10 have produced one), captures the post-bootstrap state (`argocd app list`, `kubectl get applications -A`, `kubectl get appprojects -A`), and pastes the abbreviated output into this follow-up's Completed_tasks.md entry. ## Phase 2 — Marketplace & Academy (Months 6–18)

> Phase 2 expands the manual, concierge-led Phase 1 marketplace into a self-serve product surface. Each subsection below covers one of the original placeholder areas (TS-200 / TS-210 / … / TS-310), broken into PR-sized work units with acceptance criteria and references. Tasks within a subsection are roughly ordered — dependencies on Phase 1 follow-ups are flagged inline. Numbering uses the area's tens slot (e.g., TS-200..TS-209 for self-serve onboarding) so the gap-free TS-2XX sequence mirrors the Phase 1 area-block convention (TS-040..TS-044 subscription, TS-060..TS-065 booking, etc.).

### Self-serve Provider Onboarding & Tier Automation (TS-200..TS-209)

- [ ] **TS-201-followup-1** — Live `FfmpegVideoTranscoder` adapter (`fluent-ffmpeg`)

  - Acceptance: a live `VideoTranscoderPort` implementation in `apps/workers/media-processor` probes the S3-fetched source via `ffprobe` (duration + resolution), feeds the probe into the shared `planVideoTranscode` (so the transcode-bomb caps are enforced identically to the stub), and on accept produces an HLS manifest + segments + a poster frame via `fluent-ffmpeg`, uploading them to the delivery keys `planVideoTranscode` derived. `fluent-ffmpeg` is added to `package.json` here (approved in ADR-0002 / CLAUDE.md §13); the `ffmpeg`/`ffprobe` binaries come from the OS (`apk add ffmpeg`, wired in TS-201-followup-4). Selected over the stub via an env flag mirroring the S3/ClamAV/Sharp live-mode toggles. Not unit-testable without ffmpeg on the host — lands with an integration test gated on the CI ffmpeg install.
  - References: ADR-0002; `apps/workers/media-processor/src/pipeline/adapters/stub-video-transcoder.ts` `planVideoTranscode`; CLAUDE.md §3.4, §13; TS-110-followup-2 (S3 read the transcoder consumes).

- [ ] **TS-201-followup-2** — Live job source: S3 object-created event → BullMQ → `MediaProcessingJob`

  - Acceptance: a live `JobSourcePort` consumes S3 object-created notifications (via the bucket's event config → an SQS/Redis-Streams bridge → BullMQ) and resolves each into a `MediaProcessingJob` by reading the asset row from media-svc (kind + declaredMime + declaredSizeBytes) keyed on the storage key. Replaces the Phase-1 `StubJobSource`; the `ProcessorScheduler.runOnce` claim-loop becomes a BullMQ consumer (the per-job `MediaProcessorService.process` call is unchanged). Lands once the platform BullMQ infra is wired (same gate as every other deferred worker — TS-022-followup-3 / TS-110-followup-11 shape).
  - References: ADR-0002; PDD.md §21.5 step 3; CLAUDE.md §4.3; `apps/workers/media-processor/src/pipeline/processor-scheduler.service.ts`.

Today (TS-201) the poster key is `<deliveryKey>/poster.webp` by convention + the duration is logged. Requires a service-media migration + contract regen + openapi.test/media.schema.test updates.
  - References: ADR-0002 §3; `apps/service-media/src/modules/assets/services/assets.service.ts` `computeNextState`; `packages/contracts/src/http/media.schema.ts`; PDD.md §15.1.

- [ ] **TS-206-followup-1** — Gateway BFF proxy + web-provider "Calendar sync" UI

  - Acceptance: api-gateway adds an `Adminless` provider-calendar proxy (POST connect / GET me/calendar-connection / POST sync / DELETE google) forwarding through the existing `DownstreamHttpClient` + `mapResult` shape behind `AccessTokenGuard`, plus the unauthenticated Google callback passthrough (`GET /api/v1/providers/calendar/google/callback`) that forwards `state`+`code` to service-provider and relays its 302. web-provider gains a `/dashboard/calendar` card: "Connect Google Calendar" (→ start connect → window.location = authorizationUrl), connection status (connected / error+reconnect / last-synced), "Sync now", and "Disconnect". The `GOOGLE_CALENDAR_OAUTH_REDIRECT_URI` points at the gateway callback; `GOOGLE_CALENDAR_POST_CONNECT_REDIRECT_URL` points at `/dashboard/calendar`. Twin of the TS-211-followup-1 / -2 split (service core landed first, gateway + UI follow).
  - References: TS-206 `CalendarSyncController`; `apps/api-gateway/src/modules/gateway-routes`; `apps/web-provider`; PRD.md §7.3.

- [ ] **TS-206-followup-2** — iCloud (CalDAV) + Outlook (Microsoft Graph) calendar siblings

  - Acceptance: once the Google leg is stable, add `icloud` + `outlook` to `ProviderCalendarProviderSchema` (append, never reorder) + the Prisma enum (`ALTER TYPE … ADD VALUE`); a `CalDavCalendarAdapter` (iCloud app-specific-password / CalDAV free-busy) and a `MicrosoftGraphCalendarAdapter` (Graph `getSchedule`) implement the same `GoogleCalendarPort`-shaped port (rename to `ExternalCalendarPort`), and the connection's `calendarProvider` discriminates which adapter runs. The unique index moves to `(provider_id, calendar_provider)` so a provider can link more than one. Each new provider needs its own ADR for the client library if not covered by an HTTP/CalDAV approach.
  - References: PRD.md §7.3; ADR-0003 "Follow-ups"; CLAUDE.md §13.

- [ ] **TS-206-followup-3** — Periodic background re-sync worker (BullMQ cron)

  - Acceptance: a BullMQ repeatable job (in `apps/workers`) re-pulls free/busy for every `connected` calendar connection on a cadence (e.g. every 30–60 min, jittered) so external commitments stay fresh without a manual sync. The worker calls a new internal shared-secret endpoint on service-provider (or reuses `CalendarSyncService.syncProvider` with a system actor → `provider.calendar_synced` with `actorUserId: null`). Bounded concurrency; a connection that fails auth N times flips to `error` and is skipped until reconnect. Honour Google API quota.
  - References: PDD.md §8.4 (async-first); CLAUDE.md §7.2; TS-206 `CalendarSyncService.syncProvider`.

- [ ] **TS-206-followup-4** — booking-svc availability gate consumes the external busy mirror

  - Acceptance: the future booking-svc availability gate (TS-060 / TS-204-followup-1 path) reads the provider's external busy intervals (via a gateway BFF aggregation or an internal read endpoint on service-provider — never a cross-service DB read) and rejects a booking-create whose slot overlaps an external commitment, not just the recurring windows + exceptions. The `(provider_id, starts_at)` index on `provider_availability_external` already serves the range scan.
  - References: TS-206 `provider_availability_external`; CLAUDE.md §2.3, §12; PRD.md §7.3.

- [ ] **TS-206-followup-5** — Token-refresh-failure reconsent prompt + refresh-token rotation backfill

  - Acceptance: when a sync flips a connection to `error` (Google rejected the refresh token), the web-provider portal surfaces a "Reconnect your calendar" prompt (the snapshot already carries `status: 'error'` + `lastSyncError`); reconnect re-runs the connect flow. Plus the `CALENDAR_TOKEN_ENC_KEY` rotation backfill worker (re-wrap legacy rows on a key-version bump — twin of the TS-051-followup background-check cipher backfill).
  - References: TS-206 `CalendarTokenCipherService` key-version doc; ADR-0003; CLAUDE.md §3.5.

A Playwright E2E (once TS-009e brings Playwright + Testcontainers into CI) covers provider-login → /dashboard/calendar → connect (stubbed consent) → status connected → sync → disconnect.

  - Acceptance: when the live `@elastic/elasticsearch` backend lands (TS-111-followup-1), its provider query applies an ES `exp` `function_score` decay (origin = the search `geo.center`, `scale` / `decay` calibrated so the multiplier matches the Phase-1 `geoDecayFactor` curve — `decay = 1/e` at one `SEARCH_GEO_DECAY_SCALE_KM` scale length) so the in-memory and live rankings stay aligned. The acceptance's "nearest service-area polygon" needs the doc to carry the polygon geometry (or per-area bbox) and the distance to become point-to-nearest-edge (0 when the search center falls inside any coverage polygon, else the min edge distance). Pairs with TS-202-followup-3 (polygon geometric-validity) and the `provider_service_areas` bbox already materialized in TS-202. The decay function is unchanged; only the `distanceKm` input refines.

- [ ] **TS-211-followup-3** — Per-request region resolution from geo / senior household

  - Acceptance: `InMemorySearchBackend.searchProviders` derives a region code from the inbound `SearchProvidersRequest.geo.center` (lat/lng → known bounding box) OR from the actor's senior household zip / state when no geo is supplied. Today the backend always resolves `global`; the resolver is already wired to accept a region code, so this followup is one-callsite. A small `RegionResolverService` carries the geo → region map (initially hardcoded: `nyc` bbox covers Manhattan + Brooklyn + Queens + Bronx + Staten Island; `bay_area` covers SF + Oakland + San Jose). Lands once a second region row exists in `search_ranking_config` (today only `global` is seeded). The bbox table itself can later move to a config table (TS-211-followup-3a) if ops needs to add regions without a redeploy.
  - References: `apps/service-search/src/modules/providers/services/in-memory-search-backend.service.ts` `resolved = await this.rankingConfig.resolveWeights();`; CLAUDE.md §12 (senior-data sensitivity for the household-zip path); PDD §14.1.

- [ ] **TS-211-followup-4** — Multi-replica cache-invalidation propagation

  - Acceptance: when service-search runs with > 1 replica, an upsert / delete on replica A leaves replica B's 30-second cache stale until its TTL fires. Today's in-memory TTL is correct but the per-replica divergence window is unbounded for the TTL duration. A small Redis pub/sub channel (`{env}:search-svc:ranking-config:invalidate`) carrying the mutated `regionCode` lets every replica drop its cache entry immediately. Lands once (a) service-search has > 1 replica in prod, or (b) ops reports an observable lag between weight changes and ranking effects. Bounded scope — the existing `RankingConfigService.invalidate(regionCode)` is the consumer-side hook.
  - References: CLAUDE.md §4.3 (Redis as cache; best-effort); `apps/service-search/src/modules/ranking-config/services/ranking-config.service.ts` `invalidate(regionCode)`.

Saved-search hydration now derives the FULL filter set from the stored query body (`requestToFormState(savedSearch.query, savedSearchId)`) — not just q+tier as before — so a saved "Italian-speaking certified chefs with 4.0+ rating" search re-checks every facet on load; the savedSearchUnavailable banner stays for the not_found / failure paths; the URL-side `?savedSearchId=…` hint is intentionally kept on hydration so the form refresh stays idempotent. - [ ] **TS-213-followup-1** — Live Elasticsearch `function_score` recommendation scoring calibrated to the Phase-1 weights

  - Acceptance: when the live `@elastic/elasticsearch` backend lands (TS-111-followup-1), its `recommendProviders` implementation maps the Phase-1 additive signal weights (`RECOMMENDATION_WEIGHT_*` in `in-memory-search-backend.service.ts`) onto an ES `function_score` query (terms-match boosts for language/dietary/cuisine + a filter-boost for the dementia specialty synonyms + the quality baselines), so the in-memory and live rankings + the explainability trail stay aligned. The contract output is unchanged.
  - References: PDD.md §14.1; `apps/service-search/src/modules/providers/services/in-memory-search-backend.service.ts` `scoreRecommendation`; TS-111-followup-1; TS-210-followup-1.

PII redacted at the logger + metric-label level (no seniorId / actor on labels — the signal profile is already de-identified). Joins the broader service-search observability rollout (TS-111-followup-4); mirrors TS-020-followup-1 shape.
  - References: PDD.md §20.5; CLAUDE.md §10; TS-111-followup-4.

Validates the tier-weight resolve against a live `search_ranking_config` row. (The unit suite covers the scoring against the in-memory store + a fake ranking config.)
  - References: PDD.md §24.1; CLAUDE.md §9.1; `apps/service-search/test/integration/ranking-config.integration.test.ts`.

- [ ] **TS-213-followup-5** — Richer cuisine-cue extraction (synonym taxonomy) for meal-history affinity

  - Acceptance: the gateway's `deriveCuisineCues` mines cuisine tags from memory-recipe `cuisineTag`s + a naive token split of curated preference values. Replace the token split with a synonym/taxonomy-backed extraction (pairs with TS-216's senior-care + culinary synonym dictionary) so "Tuscan" maps to "italian", "kugel" hints "jewish", etc., and the dementia-specialty synonym set (`DEMENTIA_SPECIALTY_TAGS`) moves into the same taxonomy. Improves match recall without widening the contract.

- [ ] **TS-214-followup-1** — `service-search` reads the senior preference profile for ranking personalization

  - Acceptance: the deferred half of TS-214. `service-search` (or the BFF) reads a senior's `senior_preferences` (favourite cuisine, regional tradition, language) + the operational intake tags and weights matching providers higher when their specialty / language / cuisine tags align. Overlaps heavily with TS-213 (match-recommendations) — likely lands as one shared scoring path. Needs a cross-service preference→search data flow (event-fed projection onto the discovery doc, or a gateway-side read in the search request) that does not exist today; the editor (TS-214) writes the data, this followup consumes it.
  - References: PRD.md §6.3; PDD.md §14.1; TS-213; TS-214; `apps/service-household/src/modules/seniors-directory`.

- [ ] **TS-214-followup-2** — Free-form custom-key preference editor

  - Acceptance: the TS-214 editor is a GUIDED view over a fixed 14-key curated catalog (`apps/web-family/lib/senior-preference-fields.ts`); the underlying `senior_preferences` store accepts any snake*case key. Add an "add your own" affordance so the family can capture cues outside the curated set (the PATCH merge semantics already leave custom keys untouched, so this is purely a UI surface + a key-name validator mirroring the contract's `^[a-z]a-z0-9*]\*$` floor). The save action's diff logic must widen from the curated key list to "curated keys ∪ keys currently on file" so a custom key the family clears is actually deleted.
  - References: `apps/web-family/lib/senior-preference-fields.ts`; `packages/contracts/src/http/senior-preferences.schema.ts`.

- [ ] **TS-214-followup-3** — Surface the sibling per-senior editors (intake + memory recipes) in web-family

  - Acceptance: now that `/me/seniors` + the `/seniors` directory exist, the other senior-profile backends that have NO portal UI yet — senior intake (TS-031: `PUT/GET /api/v1/seniors/:id/intake`) and memory recipes (TS-033: `/api/v1/seniors/:id/memory-recipes`) — get web-family editors hanging off `/seniors/[seniorId]/…`, plus the matching gateway proxies (none exist yet). The intake editor must respect the sensitive-vs-operational split (DOB / medical notes are encrypted server-side; the editor posts cleartext over TLS and the service re-encrypts).
  - References: PRD.md §6.1, §6.5; `apps/service-household/src/modules/intake`, `.../memory-recipes`; TS-031; TS-033.

- [ ] **TS-214-followup-4** — Testcontainers integration test for the seniors-directory endpoint

  - Acceptance: a `service-household` integration test (mirroring the established `@taste-and-see/testing` `createIsolatedDatabase` shape) boots the AppModule against real Postgres + Redis and proves `GET /api/v1/me/seniors` against the real membership / soft-delete / multi-household query: a member sees only their households' active seniors, soft-deleted seniors are excluded, removed memberships are ignored, and a user with no memberships gets `{ seniors: [] }`. The unit suite covers the service logic against a fake Prisma; the gap is the real `IN (...)` query + the `deleted_at` / `removed_at` filters under Postgres. (service-household does not yet have an integration-test harness wired — this lands it, mirroring TS-061-followup-4's first-file-in-a-service shape.)
  - References: `apps/service-household/src/modules/seniors-directory`; TS-009e-followup-2; TS-061-followup-4.

- [ ] **TS-218b-followup-1** — Sponsored-listing impression + click capture → `ads.impressions`

  - Acceptance: each rendered sponsored search row logs an impression (and a click on open) to the Cassandra `ads.impressions` keyspace bucketed by hour (PDD §8.3), attributed to the `campaignId`/`creativeId` the TS-218a resolve returned. This is the impression half of the original TS-218 acceptance, carved out because no Phase-1 Cassandra cluster exists and impression/click capture is its own task TS-275. Lands with / after TS-275. NOTE (TS-218b): the `campaignId`/`creativeId` are now carried on every sponsored hit (`SearchProvidersResponse.hits[].sponsored`) and the slot code is `search_top_tile` — the capture beacon reads them straight off the rendered row.
  - References: PRD.md §10.9; PDD.md §8.3, §18.2; TS-275.

- [ ] **TS-218b-followup-2** — Enrich the derived search audience (persona / tier / geography / cohorts)

  - Acceptance: `deriveSearchAudience()` (today returns the deliberately-empty Phase-1 audience `{ behaviorCohorts: [] }`, so only UNtargeted campaigns deliver a sponsored slot) is enriched from the viewer: persona from the actor's role, subscription `tier` (Tier 1/2/3) from service-subscription, household `geography` (region code) from service-household, and behaviour cohorts from service-analytics — each via a gateway BFF aggregation or a cross-service read at the controller boundary (no cross-service DB read, CLAUDE.md §2.3). The function takes `req.requestContext` and is a strict WIDENING of sponsored reach (targeted campaigns begin to deliver) needing no contract change (the `AdTargetingAudience` shape already carries every dimension). Today targeted campaigns never reach a search viewer (fail-closed).
  - References: `apps/service-search/src/modules/providers/services/search-audience.ts`; PDD.md §18.1; CLAUDE.md §2.3; TS-273; TS-218b.

PII discipline: provider/campaign ids stay on structured logs, never on metric labels. Mirrors the deferred TS-218a-followup-3 on the ads side.
  - References: CLAUDE.md §10; PDD.md §20.5; TS-111-followup-4; TS-218a-followup-3; TS-218b.

- [ ] **TS-220-followup-1a** — Drop the per-service-kind tier gate's reliance on the provider tier snapshot once a richer provider read lands

  - Acceptance: today `TierGatingService.evaluate` returns `provider_snapshot_unknown` before it can reach the catalog gate when service-booking's `provider_tier_snapshots` cache has no row for the assigned provider — so a brand-new (un-synced) provider booking a Tier-3 concierge kind blocks on the snapshot-missing reason rather than the catalog reason. Functionally correct in `enforce` mode (blocked either way), but in `advisory` mode the catalog violation is missed when the provider snapshot is also absent. Lands alongside TS-064's snapshot-hydration story (TS-142 event consumer for `provider.tier_changed`) so the snapshot is reliably present and the precedence question is moot.
  - References: `apps/service-booking/src/modules/tier-gating/services/tier-gating.service.ts` `evaluate` precedence; TS-064; TS-142.

- [ ] **TS-220-followup-2** — Consolidate the `ProviderTier` and `ProviderTierSnapshotTier` Prisma enums

  - Acceptance: service-booking carries two enums over the identical `basic | certified | elite` value domain — `ProviderTier` (TS-220, on `service_catalog.required_provider_tier`) and `ProviderTierSnapshotTier` (TS-064, on the per-booking provider-tier cache). They were kept separate to avoid coupling two unrelated concerns under one DB type name; once a shared `provider_tier` type is clearly the right home, fold both columns onto it (a column-type migration with the `*_old` rename dance) and drop the redundant enum.
  - References: `apps/service-booking/prisma/schema.prisma` `ProviderTier` + `ProviderTierSnapshotTier` doc-comments; CLAUDE.md §4.1.

- [ ] **TS-232-followup-7** — Fix the `AssetsService.listAssets` admin cursor off-by-one

  - Acceptance: while building TS-232 the admin `listAssets` cursor was found to anchor `nextCursor` on the **peek row** (`rows[limit]`, the first row of the next page) rather than the **last row of the current page** (`sliced[limit-1]`). Because the next-page query uses a strict `<` comparator, the peek row is then skipped — dropping one asset per page boundary. `listSeniorPhotos` was implemented with the correct last-of-page anchor (TS-232); port the same fix to `listAssets` + add a regression test proving no row is dropped across a boundary. Low urgency (admin-only surface, no test exercised the boundary today), but a real correctness bug.
  - References: `apps/service-media/src/modules/assets/services/assets.service.ts` `listAssets`; TS-110; TS-232.

  - References: PRD.md §6.4, §6.7; PDD.md §13.1; TS-070-followup-3.

- [ ] **TS-234-followup-1** — Wire the alert detectors + dispatch (missed-visit / observation-anomaly / emergency) through the subscription map + `notes`-consent gate

  - Acceptance: the three alert types TS-234 lets members subscribe to need their emitters. (a) A `missed_visit` detector — a scheduled BullMQ worker (or booking-svc event) that fires when a booked visit's accept/visit window elapses with no provider check-in. (b) The `concerning_observation` anomaly detector is TS-236. (c) The `emergency_flag` emitter is the welfare/trust-safety path (TS-302 / TS-300). Each emitter fans out to the household members subscribed to that alert type for the senior — reading `senior_alert_preferences` via the exported `SeniorAlertPreferencesService` (in-service) or a published gateway read — and dispatches through `service-notification` (TS-073) honouring each member's channel preferences. **The `concerning_observation` fan-out MUST gate observer delivery on the senior's `notes` consent** (TS-238): the subscription says the observer _wants_ the alert, but the consent says whether the senior's wellness observations may reach observers at all (the primary payer / manager is exempt — they see everything they manage). Lands as each emitter's owning task ships.
  - References: `apps/service-household/src/modules/senior-alert-preferences/`; PRD.md §6.4, §6.9; PDD.md §12.1, §12.3; CLAUDE.md §12; TS-073; TS-236; TS-300; TS-302.

PII redacted at the logger + metric-label level (seniorId / userId OK on structured logs, never on metric labels). Joins the deferred service-household + api-gateway observability rollout; mirrors the TS-020-followup-1 shape.
  - References: CLAUDE.md §10; PDD.md §20.5; TS-020-followup-1.

### Virtual Family Meal (TS-240..TS-249)

- [ ] **TS-240** — Daily.co (or LiveKit) room provisioning at booking time

  - Acceptance: on `booking.confirmed` for a virtual-family-meal-eligible booking, `service-booking` (or a sibling `service-virtual-meal`) calls Daily.co's REST API to create a time-bounded room; join URLs persisted with the booking. Provider choice (Daily.co vs LiveKit vs Twilio Video) per PDD §29 question #5 — land Daily.co as the default per PDD §13.2.
  - References: PRD.md §6.4; PDD.md §13.2, §29.

- [ ] **TS-241** — Virtual-meal scheduling UI + calendar invite delivery

  - Acceptance: `web-family` adds a "Virtual Family Meal" toggle on booking creation that prompts the payer to invite remote family by email; `.ics` calendar invites + room links delivered via `service-notification`.
  - References: PRD.md §6.4; PDD.md §12.1; TS-073.

- [ ] **TS-242** — Senior consent prompt for video recording (opt-out default)

  - Acceptance: pre-meal flow asks the senior whether the meal can be recorded; default is opt-out (CLAUDE.md §12); consent stored per-meal in the booking record.
  - References: PRD.md §11.4; CLAUDE.md §12; PDD.md §13.2.

- [ ] **TS-243** — Provider in-room host role (mute / spotlight / share recipe)

  - Acceptance: provider joins the Daily.co room as a host with elevated participant controls (mute participants, spotlight the senior, share a side-panel with the recipe being prepared). Custom in-room UI ships in `apps/web-virtual-meal` (or a route within web-family).
  - References: PRD.md §6.4; PDD.md §13.2.

- [ ] **TS-244** — In-meal translation assistance for multilingual households

  - Acceptance: optional in-meal chat with translation (English / Spanish / Mandarin) via the same translation API used in messaging (PDD §13.1). Senior-mode large-text rendering.
  - References: PRD.md §6.7, §11.5; PDD.md §13.1.

- [ ] **TS-245** — Non-intrusive presence indicators (wave / show food / cheers)

  - Acceptance: simple emoji-reaction overlay (wave / heart / cheers / show-food) so seniors with limited fine motor control or hearing can engage without typing. Senior-mode tap targets ≥ 48px (CLAUDE.md §8.3).
  - References: PRD.md §6.4, §11.5; CLAUDE.md §8.3.

- [ ] **TS-246** — Recording consent flow + S3 storage with time-bounded retention

  - Acceptance: when consent is granted (TS-242), recording lands in S3 via Daily.co's recording webhook; a `virtual_meal_recordings` table tracks the asset; default 90-day retention with explicit family opt-in for longer; signed URLs only.
  - References: PRD.md §11.4; PDD.md §13.2, §21.3; TS-242.

- [ ] **TS-247** — Senior-mode video UI (large buttons / simplified controls / captions on by default)

  - Acceptance: senior-side join screen renders a large-button join, minimal controls (audio toggle, leave), captions on by default. Honours the senior-mode flag (CLAUDE.md §8.3).
  - References: PRD.md §11.5; PDD.md §6.3; CLAUDE.md §8.3.

- [ ] **TS-248** — Graceful bandwidth degradation (audio-only fallback)

  - Acceptance: Daily.co's adaptive simulcast configured to drop to audio-only when bandwidth falls below threshold; in-UI banner explains the degradation to the senior in plain language.
  - References: PRD.md §11.5; PDD.md §13.2.

- [ ] **TS-249** — Daily.co webhook handlers for room lifecycle events

  - Acceptance: `service-webhook` accepts Daily.co webhooks (room.joined, recording.started, recording.completed) with signature verification (mirrors the Stripe pattern in PDD §11.1 / CLAUDE.md §3.5); events flow to `service-booking` for meal-attendance analytics + `service-analytics`.
  - References: PRD.md §6.4; PDD.md §7.3; CLAUDE.md §3.5.

- [ ] **TS-260-followup-1** — Compute LTV + CAC (today null)

  - Acceptance: `saas_metrics_daily.ltv` + `.cac` are nullable + NULL in Phase 1 because neither is derivable from the accounting ledger alone — LTV needs a stable churn-rate denominator (annualised from the daily churn series) and CAC needs sales/marketing-spend attribution per acquired customer. Once a sales/marketing expense sub-account exists in the chart of accounts (CAC = trailing-period S&M expense ÷ new subscriptions) and the churn series is long enough to annualise (LTV = ARPU × gross-margin ÷ churn-rate), `SaasMetricsService` populates both columns. The wire shape already carries `ltvMinor` / `cacMinor` (nullable) so this is additive.
  - References: `apps/service-accounting/src/modules/saas-metrics/services/saas-metrics.service.ts` `ltv: null` / `cac: null`; PRD.md §10.3; PDD.md §23.2.

- [ ] **TS-260-followup-2** — Per-customer-group metrics breakdown (family / provider / academy)

  - Acceptance: TS-260 aggregates MRR across all customer groups into one daily row. Add a per-group breakdown (a `customer_group` discriminator column on a sibling table, or group sub-totals on the daily row) so the dashboard can split family-subscription MRR from provider-subscription MRR from academy-membership MRR. The per-subscription snapshot (`saas_subscription_mrr_daily`) already carries `customer_group`, so the breakdown is a roll-up over data already persisted.
  - References: `apps/service-accounting/src/modules/saas-metrics/services/saas-metrics.service.ts`; PRD.md §5; PDD.md §23.2.

Twin of TS-022-followup-3c (identity-janitor) — lands with the broader per-service build rollout (TS-009g-followup-4).
  - References: `apps/workers/accounting-metrics/README.md`; PDD.md §20.1, §20.2; TS-009g-followup-4; TS-022-followup-3c.

  - Acceptance: `SaasMetricsService` + the controller emit a span per compute + counters (`saas_metrics_computed_total`, `saas_metrics_active_subscriptions`, `saas_metrics_non_usd_skipped_total`); the worker's orchestrator emits a `saas_metrics_run_total{outcome=ok|failed}` counter + the `mrr_minor` gauge. PII-free labels. Mirrors the TS-020-followup-1 shape; joins the accounting-svc observability rollout.
  - References: CLAUDE.md §10; PDD.md §20.5; TS-020-followup-1.

- [ ] **TS-260-followup-5** — Testcontainers integration test: full TS-260 round-trip against a real Postgres

  - Acceptance: a service-accounting integration test boots the AppModule against an ephemeral Postgres, seeds a few `deferred_revenue_balances` rows, POSTs the internal compute endpoint, and asserts the `saas_metrics_daily` row + the per-subscription snapshot land with the expected MRR / movement, then asserts a second-day compute decomposes new/expansion/contraction/churn against the prior snapshot. Validates the migration + the `$transaction` upsert against a live Postgres (the unit suite uses a FakePrisma). Mirrors the TS-082 / TS-211-followup-5 integration shape.
  - References: PDD.md §24.1; CLAUDE.md §9.1; `packages/testing` harness (TS-009e-followup-1).

- [ ] **TS-260-followup-6** — Batched / streamed active-balance read for scale

  - Acceptance: `SaasMetricsService.computeForDate` reads every active covering balance in a single `findMany`. At Year-2 scale (PDD §27 — 8K households + provider/academy subs) that's still small, but the read is unbounded. Page the balance scan (cursor on `id`) + accumulate the per-subscription MRR map incrementally so the compute's memory + lock footprint stays flat regardless of subscriber count. Mirrors the `DEFAULT_SWEEP_BATCH_SIZE` paging in `SubscriptionRevenueRecognizerService.recognizeDaily`.
  - References: `apps/service-accounting/src/modules/saas-metrics/services/saas-metrics.service.ts` balance `findMany`; PDD.md §27; CLAUDE.md §7.2.

- [ ] **TS-282-followup-5** — Public media URL convention for assetKeys — **DECOMPOSED 2026-07-28 into 5a / 5b / 5c. Do not work this entry.**

  - Original acceptance: a public URL scheme (CDN or media-svc public route) for resolving media assetKeys on unauthenticated surfaces; unblocks OG/Twitter card images and author byline photos on the public blog (both currently omitted).
  - **Why decomposed — the task asks for a URL convention for a KEY convention that does not exist.** Scoping found five things:
    1. **`assetKey` is an unvalidated bounded string.** `AssetKeySchema` in `ads-campaign.schema.ts` is `z.string().trim().min(1).max(...)` and nothing more; `content.authors.photo_asset_key` and the article SEO image fields are the same shape. The doc-comments say these "reference media-svc S3 assets", and **nothing enforces it, nothing validates it, and no code anywhere resolves one.** It could be a media asset id, an S3 storage key, or a typo — all three are currently valid. There is no URL to define until the key means something.
    2. **Media delivery today is a SHORT-LIVED SIGNED URL minted per read** (`signedDeliveryUrl` on `MediaAssetResponse`, null unless `status = ready`). That is incompatible with OG / Twitter cards _by construction_: a crawler fetches the image hours or days after the HTML was rendered, and web-marketing's ISR caches that HTML for 300s. The public path can never be "put the signed URL in the meta tag" — it has to be a stable URL that redirects to a freshly minted one, or a genuine CDN origin.
    3. **There is no public-visibility concept on a media asset, and the asset-kind enum is `senior_photo | provider_profile_photo | provider_video_intro | memory_recipe_image | provider_document | certification_evidence | academy_lesson_attachment`.** A generic public read over assetKeys turns media-svc into an open read proxy for seniors' photos and statutory background-check evidence. **A publication flag is mandatory, not a refinement** — and "referenced by a published article" is NOT a sufficient gate, because it lets an editor publish any key they can paste into a field.
    4. **There is no asset kind for editorial imagery at all.** A blog author photo and an article social card have no `MediaAssetKind` to be uploaded as, so today they cannot be created through the media pipeline even in principle. Whatever convention lands, this enum grows first.
    5. **The AUTHENTICATED half of the problem is separable and unblocked.** `web-admin`'s ad-creative detail page renders `creative.assetKeys.join(', ')` as literal text — so the reviewer approving a creative _for accessibility_ (alt text, contrast, motion) in the shipped TS-277a workflow **cannot see the image they are approving**. That needs no public URL at all: the caller is authenticated, and signed delivery URLs already exist.
  - References: TS-282-followup-3; TS-277a (the creative-review workflow that cannot see its creatives); PDD.md §13; `apps/service-media/prisma/schema.prisma`; `packages/contracts/src/http/media.schema.ts`.

  - Acceptance: carved from TS-282-followup-5a. The enum is `senior_photo | provider_profile_photo | provider_video_intro | memory_recipe_image | provider_document | certification_evidence | academy_lesson_attachment` — there is nothing a blog author photo or an article social card could be uploaded AS, so the content track's `photoAssetKey` / `ogImageKey` / `twitterImageKey` fields can only ever hold keys minted outside the media pipeline. Add the kind(s) with their per-kind MIME allow-list and size cap (an expand-only enum migration in service-media plus the contract mirror), and decide the owner scope: these assets belong to no household, senior or provider, so they need either a `content` scope kind or an explicit platform-scope convention.
  - Land it WITH TS-282-followup-5c rather than before it: a kind with no upload surface and no consumer is dead enum surface, and the scope-kind question is the same question 5c's publication flag has to answer.
  - References: TS-282-followup-5 (the decomposition, finding 4); TS-282-followup-5a; `apps/service-media/prisma/schema.prisma`; CLAUDE.md §3.4.

- [ ] **TS-282-followup-5c** — Public media URLs — **USER-BLOCKED on one decision**

  - Acceptance: OG / Twitter card images and public author byline photos resolve on anonymous surfaces. Requires, in order: TS-282-followup-5a's key convention; a **publication flag on the asset** (per finding 3 — without it this route is an open read proxy for seniors' photos and background-check evidence, and it must be an explicit act on the asset, never inferred from "an article references it"); and then the delivery mechanism.
  - **The decision only the user can make** is the mechanism, and the options are not equivalent:
    - **(a) media-svc public redirect** — `GET /api/v1/public/media/{assetKey}` 302s to a freshly minted signed URL. Bucket stays private, no new infrastructure, works with crawlers, cacheable at the edge later. Costs a hop per image. **Recommended for Phase 1** — it needs nothing that is not already deployed.
    - **(b) public CDN origin** — a public-read bucket or prefix that published assets are copied into, fronted by a CDN. Faster and cheaper at scale; needs CDN provisioning (currently blocked on live Contabo credentials, per the deployability state) and introduces a second copy of every published asset whose deletion path has to be built too.
  - Do not pick silently (CLAUDE.md §16). Note that the two differ in what "unpublish" means: (a) is instant, (b) has to purge.
  - References: TS-282-followup-5 (the decomposition); TS-282-followup-1 (the omitted OG images); TS-283-followup-3 (the omitted byline photos); CLAUDE.md §3.4, §12.

Also corrected the base's header comment, which said the site "has no required server env": it has no SECRET env, which is a different claim and is why the Secret-less shape is still right. Base renders 9 kinds. **Filed TS-289-followup-3** — `NEXT_PUBLIC_DISQUS_SHORTNAME` appears in NO workflow and NO manifest, so blog comments are silently dark in every environment; same failure shape as this task and it needs a BUILD arg, not a ConfigMap key.); see Completed_tasks.md. -->

- [ ] **TS-289-followup-3** — `NEXT_PUBLIC_DISQUS_SHORTNAME` is wired nowhere, so blog comments are dark in every environment

  - Acceptance: found while closing TS-282-followup-6. The string appears in no GitHub workflow and no k8s manifest, so `resolveDisqusEmbed` (TS-289-followup-1) evaluates to "off" in dev, staging and prod alike — the consent card never renders and the comments section announces nothing. **It is NOT a ConfigMap key**: `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` is inlined by Next.js at BUILD time, so it must be a `--build-arg` in `web-marketing-build.yml` (and therefore a repository/environment variable), which also means a per-environment shortname requires a per-environment image. Decide that first: one shortname across all envs and a single image, or per-env builds. The Phase-1 answer is probably one shortname with comments enabled only on prod's host, which is a product call rather than a wiring one.
  - Note the sibling gap this shares with TS-289-followup-1's own findings: web-marketing has **no CSP**, and whatever CSP eventually lands must allow the Disqus origins or the embed breaks in a way that looks like a Disqus outage.
  - References: TS-289-followup-1; TS-282-followup-6; `apps/web-marketing/lib/comments.ts`; `.github/workflows/web-marketing-build.yml`.

  - References: TS-282-followup-3; `apps/service-content/src/modules/public-blog/`.

     New `booking_held_check_in_total{kind,decision}` counter — its own instrument on purpose, because an allowed held check-out is an `applied` transition and would be invisible in the very funnel that counts completions. `{check_out, allowed}` is the safety-relevant series.
     A completion under hold does NOT clear the hold (the hold belongs to the incident and is released when the incident closes; a completion is not a closure) — asserted.

- [ ] **TS-302e-followup-1** — Route a completed-under-hold visit back to the incident

  - Acceptance: TS-302e deliberately ALLOWS a check-out on a held booking (refusing would destroy the record of a visit that demonstrably happened), and records the fact as a WARN log plus the `booking_held_check_in_total{kind="check_out",decision="allowed"}` counter. Neither reaches the trust & safety operator working the incident that placed the hold — so the fact that a suspended visit went ahead anyway, which is exactly the kind of thing a welfare review needs, lives only in a log stream and a dashboard nobody is required to look at.
  - The shape: a `booking.completed_under_hold` outbox event from service-booking (NOT a field on `booking.completed` — its consumer is the accounting recognizer, and making trust-safety subscribe to every completion to find the rare one is the wrong fan-out), consumed by service-trust-safety's outbox-consumer module, which annotates the incident. **The blocker is that last step: there is no incident-annotation mechanism.** `incidents.system_facts` (TS-308c-followup-2) is written once at incident birth by a detector and is a discriminated union keyed on `detector`; appending a post-hoc fact to an existing incident is a different write and needs its own decision. Settle that first — it is the same gap TS-304-followup-2's re-grade path will hit.
  - References: TS-302e; TS-304; TS-308c-followup-2; `apps/service-booking/src/modules/check-ins/services/check-ins.service.ts`.

- [ ] **TS-304-followup-2** — Hold on triage RE-GRADE, not just on open

  - Acceptance: TS-304's hold rides the incident OPEN and RESOLVE transitions only. An incident that arrives `medium` and is re-graded to `high` by TS-302 triage does NOT retroactively request a hold — the gap is real, documented in `booking-hold-policy.ts`, and deliberately not papered over with a booking-side severity check (which would put a second copy of the hold predicate in the service with the least context to own it). The fix belongs on the trust-safety side: a re-grade path that consults `isBookingHoldEligible` on the new severity and emits `.requested` if it now qualifies (and, symmetrically, decides whether a downgrade should release — probably NOT, since a downgrade is a triage judgement, not a closure). Blocked on TS-302's re-grade surface existing at all.
  - References: TS-304; TS-302; `apps/service-trust-safety/src/modules/incidents/booking-hold-policy.ts`.

- [ ] **TS-305c-followup-1a** — Trigram index for the provider name search

  - Acceptance: `GET /api/v1/admin/providers?q=` filters with `display_name ILIKE '%q%'`, which no btree can serve — it is a sequential scan. That is correct today (the table is ~200 rows at Year-1 per PRD §12.2, `limit` caps at 100, and the route is admin-gated so the call rate is human-paced) and it is documented in `ProviderDirectoryService`'s doc-block, but it degrades linearly with the roster. The fix is a `pg_trgm` GIN index on `providers.display_name`. Held off deliberately: `CREATE EXTENSION pg_trgm` is an infrastructure decision (it needs the privilege on the managed instance and it applies database-wide), not a query-shape one, so it wants its own migration review rather than riding a feature PR. Land it when the provider count crosses ~2,000 or when the directory shows up in a slow-query report. The same question will apply to any future substring search on a growing table — worth an ADR at that point rather than a second one-off.
  - References: TS-305c-followup-1; `apps/service-provider/src/modules/directory/services/provider-directory.service.ts` (the doc-block that records the trade); CLAUDE.md §7.3; `apps/service-provider/prisma/schema.prisma`.

- [ ] **TS-305d-followup-1** — Validate the metrics window and the sample floor against a real corpus

  - Acceptance: `PROVIDER_METRICS_WINDOW_DAYS` (90) and `PROVIDER_METRICS_MIN_SAMPLE` (5) are reasoned
    defaults, not measured ones — there is no booking history on this platform to measure against yet. Once
    there is, check both against it: if most active providers sit in `insufficient_data` on the recent
    window, the window is too short or the floor too high and the panel says nothing to the people it was
    built for; if a provider with two bad months reads as `measured` and fine, the window is too long to
    describe the present. Same shape of debt as TS-300-followup-3's SLA budgets, TS-308a-followup-2's speed
    ceiling and TS-308c-followup-1's thresholds — worth doing as one pass over all four.
  - References: TS-305d; `packages/contracts/src/http/provider-metrics.schema.ts` (the doc-blocks stating
    the reasoning); TS-300-followup-3; CLAUDE.md §10.

  - Acceptance: live-Postgres cases for the half unit tests cannot reach. (1) The `COALESCE` upsert: apply

- [ ] **TS-305d-followup-2b1a** — The 30 boot-graph guards still compile without decorator metadata

  - TS-305d-followup-2b1 converted the 8 integration configs. The unit configs — and with them every
    `test/app-module-graph.test.ts` — still run on esbuild, so **the boot guards still read a bare-param
    provider as zero-dependency and report success without attempting the resolution.** That is precisely
    how service-subscription shipped a module that could not boot with 188 green tasks.
  - It is not urgent in the way that entry was: the `dist/`-boot sweep run on 2026-08-07 proved all 30
    workloads resolve today, so nothing is currently hidden. It is the _next_ one this would miss.
  - Why it was not done in the same pass: each app's `vitest.config.ts` covers the unit suite as well as the
    boot guard (`include: ['src/**/*.test.ts', 'test/app-module-graph.test.ts']`), so enabling the plugin
    there compiles **every** unit test with TypeScript — slower on the lane that runs on every change, and it
    will surface however many suites currently depend, knowingly or not, on injection being absent (several
    construct providers directly _because_ of this limitation — see the comments in
    `service-provider/src/modules/outbox-consumers/outbox-consumers.module.ts`, `packages/nest-audit`,
    `packages/nest-pagerduty`, `packages/nest-bullmq-scheduler`). That surfacing is the point, but it is the
    whole cost of the task and should be planned, not discovered.
  - Shape: either a second vitest project for the boot guard alone (narrow, fast, gets the property that
    matters) or the plugin on the whole unit lane (complete, slower). **Prefer the first** — the property
    worth having is "the DI graph resolves", and it does not need the unit suite to pay for it.
  - Acceptance: deleting a required `imports:` entry from any service's module makes that service's
    boot-graph guard fail — demonstrated by re-injecting exactly the service-subscription defect
    (`imports: [SubscriptionsModule]`) and watching it go red.
  - References: TS-305d-followup-2b1; TS-506; `packages/testing/vitest-plugin.cjs`;
    `packages/testing/src/boot/app-module-graph.ts`; CLAUDE.md §9.1

- [ ] **TS-305d-followup-2b1c** — service-identity's IP circuit breaker: four failures on the bucket count

  - The last of the failures TS-305d-followup-2b1b surfaced, carved out because it is a different problem
    from the other five and needs its own diagnosis rather than being lumped in.
  - `test/integration/ip-circuit-breaker.integration.test.ts` fails 4 of its cases, all on the Redis bucket
    count: `expected 3 to be 5` and `expected 4 to be 5` against `BREAKER_THRESHOLD`. The other five suites
    in service-identity are green, so the fleet, the env and the DI graph are all fine — this is the
    breaker's own arithmetic or the suite's model of it.
  - **Diagnose before assuming it is the test.** The named case is "per-IP isolation: a different IP is not
    blocked even when a sibling IP is fully tripped", and an under-count there could mean the breaker stops
    incrementing once it trips — which would be a real defect with a security shape (§3.1's IP-level circuit

- Acceptance: discovered while building TS-306-followup-1a and it is bigger than that sweep. The service has **no `@taste-and-see/tracing` dependency, no `ObservabilityModule` in its composition root, and no `initMetrics` in `main.ts`** — so workload #28 emits no metrics and no traces, against CLAUDE.md §10's "every service emits". The sweep's metrics class was written and then deleted rather than shipped: `getMeter` returns a usable no-op when the SDK was never initialised, so it would have compiled, run, and reported nothing while reading as instrumentation — worse than the honest gap. Wire the service the way every other one is (`ObservabilityModule.forRoot({ serviceName })` + the bootstrap in `main.ts`), then add the instruments the existing surfaces have earned: the SLA-breach sweep's breached / due-soon gauges, incidents opened by source and severity, and the pager's outcome counter. Check `service-ads` and `service-content` for the same gap while there — they are the other two post-fleet stragglers (TS-300-followup-2) and may share it.
